detail.abstract: I explore the magnitude and heterogeneous effects of menu costs on pricing dynamics. To do so, I develop a dynamic discrete choice model of a firm facing menu costs when adjusting prices, using methods from industrial organization. I obtain descriptive evidence that is consistent with the model using scanner data from grocery stores in the US. I then estimate the model and find that the menu cost is substantial, amounting to 7.2% of overall retail profit at the average-sized retailer. When applied to a high-inflation scenario, the model generates an increase in both frequency and magnitude of price changes. In addition, as the menu cost varies little with the retailers' size, smaller retailers face a higher burden of the menu costs. Being unable to adjust prices frequently, they exhibit earlier and more pronounced responses to anticipated cost increases.

title: A Note on Optimal Product Pricing
affiliations: and Stanford University - Department of Electrical Engineering

detail.title: A Note on Optimal Product Pricing
detail.abstract: We consider the problem of choosing prices of a set of products so as to maximize profit, taking into account self-elasticity and cross-elasticity, subject to constraints on the prices. We show that this problem can be formulated as maximizing the sum of a convex and concave function. We compare three methods for finding a locally optimal approximate solution. The first is based on the convex-concave procedure, and involves solving a short sequence of convex problems. Another one uses a custom minorizemaximize method, and involves solving a sequence of quadratic programs. The final method is to use a general purpose nonlinear programming method. In numerical examples all three converge reliably to the same local maximum, independent of the starting prices, leading us to believe that the prices found are likely globally optimal.

detail.abstract: The purpose of this quantitative correlations study is to investigate factors influencing consumer purchase decisions for tires for new entrants' decision- making. This research serves three purposes. The focus will be the role of demographic influences that interact consumers with ethnocentrism and the factors at the actual point of purchase. The author analyzes the direct effect on actual purchase from five (5) factors of gender, age, educational level, income level, and political leaning. The controlling factors of warranty and free tire services are also noted in the model. The sample included 2945 respondents who participated in a survey conducted from August to September 2017. Analysis also included regional national voting patterns and the zip code where the purchases were finally made. Data analysis was conducted using SPSS v26 to include descriptive statistics, binomial logistic regression analysis, and correlations. The findings point towards certain trends in consumer behavior that are directly influenced by demographic characteristics. The data presents a pattern of actual purchase that contradicts the existing literature concerning age, gender, and this study's own initial hypothesis of gender, age, and political party affiliation. The results of the study, which reflect purchase patterns, should be guided with certain limitations. Tires presumed to be American made or manufactured in the USA quite possibly are made overseas. Furthermore, these implications have strong considerations for the diversification into the American market by foreign investment because the findings demonstrate that demographic factors such as age and gender influence consumer purchase decisions.

detail.abstract: The pandemic accelerated the adoption of contactless payment methods, and many consumers replaced cash payments with mobile payments. This paper aimed to study how economicrational (perceived usefulness and ease of use), existential (perceived risk of contamination), and institutional (social influence and retail support) factors influenced the acceptance of mobile payment during the pandemic. Empirical data were collected via an online survey in Central-Eastern Europe in 2021, resulting in a sample of 545. The Structural Equation Modelling revealed that social influence and retail support (institutional factors) contributed much more to consumers' mobile payment acceptance during the pandemic than the existential factor, the perceived risk of cash payment. The impact of the economic-rational factors (perceived usefulness and ease of use) on mobile payment acceptance was confirmed. Our research concept integrated institutional factors, such as retail support, in the technology acceptance model, which had theoretical and business implications.

detail.title: Analysis of Online Customer Reviews for Product Insights
detail.abstract: This project studies how online customer reviews affect people’s buying decisions and how businesses can use these reviews to improve their products and services. Nowadays, most customers read reviews before making a purchase, and these opinions strongly influence trust, satisfaction, and brand reputation. The study collected data from 100 online shoppers through a questionnaire and analyzed it using statistical and data science methods like correlation, regression, and sentiment analysis. The results show that positive reviews increase sales and build trust, while negative reviews reduce purchase chances. Important factors found in reviews include product quality, delivery experience, and price fairness. The research also highlights how companies can turn customer feedback into useful insights for improving quality, marketing strategies, and customer service. Overall, this study proves that analyzing online reviews is an effective way for businesses to make better, data-driven decisions and build stronger customer relationships.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to reshape labor markets, yet causal evidence remains scarce. We exploit a novel Swedish subsidy program that encouraged small and mid-sized firms to adopt AI. Using a synthetic difference-in-differences design comparing awarded and non-awarded firms, we find that AI subsidies led to a sustained increase in job postings over five years, but with no statistically detectable change in employment. This pattern reflects hiring signals concentrated in AI occupations and white-collar roles. Our findings align with task-based models of automation, in which AI adoption reconfigures work and spurs demand for new skills, but hiring frictions and the need for complementary investments delay workforce expansion.

title: Product Design under Consumer Rebellion and Preference Uncertainty
affiliations: South China University of Technology - School of Business Administration (SBA), Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) - Department of Information Systems and Management Engineering, School of Business Administration, South China University of Technology and University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management

detail.title: Product Design under Consumer Rebellion and Preference Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Firms increasingly face markets where consumers seek to express individuality by rebelling against mainstream tastes. Yet how consumer rebellion shapes firms’ product design and differentiation remains unclear, especially when consumer preferences are uncertain. To shed some light on this, we develop a game-theoretic model. We find that the impact of rebellion on product differentiation is non-monotonic: as rebellion strengthens, differentiation first decreases but then increases. This U-shaped relationship arises from the tension between the direct stimulating effect of stronger consumer rebellion on firms’ incentives to differentiate and the indirect curb on the effect of preference uncertainty. Firms’ expected prices and profits also exhibit non-monotonic patterns, driven both by changes in differentiation and by shifts in price competition intensity. By contrast, consumer surplus follows an inverted U-shaped pattern, first increasing and then decreasing. Compared to markets without social influence, rebellion can enhance either firm profits or consumer surplus. However, under certain conditions, it will lead to a lose-lose situation—reducing firm profits and consumer surplus simultaneously.

detail.abstract:
We present a complete mathematical framework for human perception based on three foundational principles: (1) all physical phenomena consist of continuous oscillatory processes that must be discretized for conscious access, (2) perception operates through gas molecular information dynamics where perceptual elements behave as thermodynamic information molecules achieving equilibrium through Gibbs free energy minimization, and (3) cross-modal integration occurs through Biological Maxwell Demon (BMD) coordinate equivalence rather than computational fusion. 

The framework resolves fundamental paradoxes in perception science through rigorous mathematical proof. We establish why perceptual capacity is unbounded (Theorem \ref{thm:unbounded_capacity}), how cross-modal integration occurs instantaneously (Theorem \ref{thm:instantaneous_integration}), why memory storage is unnecessary for perception (Theorem \ref{thm:storage_elimination}), and how consciousness maintains continuity through predetermined frame selection (Theorem \ref{thm:predetermined_frames}). Each result is derived from first principles using thermodynamic necessity arguments, information-theoretic constraints, and dynamical systems analysis.

We formalize visual perception through thermodynamic pixel entities exhibiting gas molecular behavior with entropy-based processing allocation. Auditory perception is formalized through acoustic pattern space navigation with zero-computation recognition proofs. Chemical perception is formalized through molecular information catalysis with dual-functionality architectures achieving therapeutic amplification factors exceeding $10^3$. The BMD Equivalence Theorem (Theorem \ref{thm:bmd_equivalence}) proves that all sensory modalities resolve to identical consciousness coordinates, enabling instant cross-modal combination through coordinate identity.

The framework integrates evolutionary context through game-theoretic analysis of fire circle selection pressures, demonstrating that extended observation (4-6 hours), enhanced scrutiny conditions, and consistent grouping created unprecedented selection for collective naming systems and beauty-credibility coupling mechanisms. We prove conversation operates through the same gas molecular principles as perception, enabling reverse BMD state inference and causal chain establishment through minimal variance communication (Theorem \ref{thm:minimal_variance}).

Empirical validation includes the 95\%/5\% visual memory architecture, audio-pharmaceutical BMD equivalence validated through neurofunk pattern recognition ($p < 10^{-23}$), dream state BMD fabrication dynamics, and cross-cultural universals in collective naming convergence. The framework enables practical applications in conscious AI design through BMD coordinate navigation algorithms, therapeutic consciousness optimization through multi-modal BMD pathway targeting, and enhanced social coordination through fire circle optimization principles.

This work provides the first complete, rigorous mathematical foundation for human perception as a unified phenomenon operating through gas molecular information processing on oscillatory substrates via BMD coordinate navigation.

detail.title: Comparative Performance of Gradient Boosting and Random Forest for Smart Home Device Classification
detail.abstract: The proliferation of IoT devices in smart environments has brought significant challenges related to device management, security, and communication integrity. Effective classification and recognition of these devices are crucial for enhancing management processes, strengthening security protocols, and ensuring seamless communication. This study compares Gradient Boosting (GB) and Random Forest (RF) classifiers using a dataset containing network traffic data from 1,900 smart home devices. The classifiers were evaluated based on their ability to categorize devices into ten distinct categories, each representing a specific type or function of IoT devices. Utilizing performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, MCC (Matthews Correlation Coefficient), F1-score, and AUC (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve), both models demonstrated strong classification capabilities through 20-fold cross-validation.Results indicated that Gradient Boosting achieved a precision of 92%, recall of 90%, and an F1-score of 91%, slightly outperforming Random Forest, which recorded a precision of 89%, recall of 87%, and an F1-score of 88%. However, Random Forest demonstrated superior performance in AUC with a score of 0.94, excelling in distinguishing specific device types. Both models encountered challenges in classifying devices with overlapping features, underscoring the necessity for further feature refinement and tuning. The ROC curve analysis provided insights into the actual positive rate versus false positive rate trade-offs, while confusion matrices highlighted specific categories where misclassifications occurred. This study underscores the potential of integrating advanced machine learning techniques to improve IoT device classification and facilitate smarter, more secure environments

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has immense potential to enhance teaching and learning by personalizing education, supporting teachers, and improving student outcomes. However, making AI tools widely accessible in educational institutions, especially in developing contexts like Ghana, faces significant challenges. This paper examines the need for AI-powered educational assistants for students in Ghana and analyzes the barriers preventing widespread deployment of such AI models in schools. Key challenges identified include high computational costs and infrastructure constraints, limited internet connectivity, lack of AI literacy among educators, and ethical and policy concerns. Drawing on recent research and case studies (including efforts to optimize AI models for wider access), we discuss how these obstacles hinder AI integration in middle and high schools. Finally, we propose strategies and recommendations to overcome these barriers so that students and teachers can effectively leverage AI for personalized learning. By addressing economic, technical, and institutional challenges, Ghana's education system can harness AI's benefits to improve learning outcomes and equity.

title: On the Categorical Construction of Temporal Experience : A Mathematical Investigation of Discrete Observer Systems and Continuous Physical Processes

detail.title: On the Categorical Construction of Temporal Experience : A Mathematical Investigation of Discrete Observer Systems and Continuous Physical Processes
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the mathematical foundations underlying temporal experience in physical systems. Through analysis of nite computational systems interacting with continuous physical processes, we examine how discrete categorization mechanisms might contribute to the construction of temporal ordering. We propose a framework wherein temporal experience emerges from the rate-limiting dynamics of categorical state assignment rather than thermodynamic entropy maximization. The analysis suggests that irreversibility may arise from computational constraints in discrete observer systems rather than fundamental physical asymmetries. Mathematical models are developed to formalize these relationships, and implications for understanding temporal directionality are discussed.

title: AI Slop and Data Pollution in the Age of Generative AI: Strategic Risks, Economic Consequences, and Governance Pathways for Business, Management, and the Creative Industries

detail.title: AI Slop and Data Pollution in the Age of Generative AI: Strategic Risks, Economic Consequences, and Governance Pathways for Business, Management, and the Creative Industries

keywords: AI Slop Business and Management Implications

detail.abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced a new form of digital waste commonly termed AI slop: a deluge of low-originality, self-referential synthetic outputs that increasingly contaminate online information ecosystems. As generative systems recursively train on their own by-products, a compounding feedback loop of degraded semantics and homogenized patterns emerges, threatening the epistemic, economic, and cultural integrity of AI-enabled societies. Recent studies reveal that by May 2025, approximately 52% of new online articles were machine-generated, while human-authored content still dominated high-ranking search and conversational responses, comprising about 86% of top Google results and 82% of sources cited by large-language-model (LLM) answer engines. This quantitative saturation signifies not only a data-quality crisis but also an emergent governance challenge for enterprises, policymakers, and creators. This paper investigates how AI slop and synthetic data pollution jointly erode information value, distort model reliability, and destabilize creative and decision-making ecosystems. Integrating insights from computer science, management, and information governance, it conceptualizes the phenomenon as a self-reinforcing cycle linking data scarcity, model collapse, and societal disinformation. The analysis further explores mitigation pathways-ranging from human-in-the-loop oversight and hybrid data curation to provenance tagging, auditing, and ethical policy frameworks, to safeguard the long-term sustainability of the data commons. The study contributes an interdisciplinary framework for understanding and managing AI slop as both a technical failure mode and a socioeconomic governance issue of the digital age.

title: Designing an Application Based on VTO, GenAI, AR/VR, and Sustainability in Online Fashion Retail: A Conceptual Framework and Practical Illustration

detail.title: Designing an Application Based on VTO, GenAI, AR/VR, and Sustainability in Online Fashion Retail: A Conceptual Framework and Practical Illustration
detail.abstract: In recent years, online fashion retail has witnessed substantial expansion, driven primarily by consumers' time constraints, limited access to physical outlets, and external factors such as health crises. However, despite these advantages, online shopping continues to face significant challenges, including the lack of a tangible fitting experience, high return rates, and persistent customer distrust. To address these shortcomings, this study introduces a conceptual framework that integrates Virtual Try-On (VTO), Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), Augmented and Virtual Reality (AR/VR), and sustainability practices. Within this framework, VTO mitigates purchase uncertainty, GenAI enhances personalization, AR/VR foster immersive shopping experiences, and sustainability information strengthens brand credibility. The central outcome of this research is the design of an innovative application that unifies these technologies into a single system. To illustrate its practical relevance, the study presents an applied example drawn from the H&M online platform. Theoretically, the framework is grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Customer Experience (CX) framework, Dynamic Capabilities View (DCV), and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). Practically, it offers actionable insights for fashion retailers, contributing to enhanced customer engagement and strengthened digital competitiveness.

detail.abstract: The Artificial Intelligence Act (AIA) is connected to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in several significant ways. Some of these connections appear to hint towards a convergence (be it the partial concomitance of their goals, the presence of some shared notions, the reliance on some similar mechanisms), whereas others are rather divergences, or point at least towards a clear separation, as well as a recurrent distancing. The overall picture drawn by the AIA and the GDPR might look like a series of intersecting zigzagging lines and trompe l’oeil resemblances, potentially inducing some confusion. This contribution offers a series of pointers to better understand what exactly is at stake in this not straightforward – but crucial - relationship.

title: Incumbent's Advantage via Expertise Asymmetry: Revitalization of the Chinese Pearl Industry with Livestreaming

detail.title: Incumbent's Advantage via Expertise Asymmetry: Revitalization of the Chinese Pearl Industry with Livestreaming

detail.abstract: This study examines how incumbents in mature industries can revitalize their industries amid technologically adept entrants. Using a longitudinal qualitative study of China's pearl industry (2017-2024), we trace how incumbent pearl firms and livestreaming-first entrants (LSFs) interacted as livestreaming transformed the industry. Drawing on ethnographic, interview, and archival data, we find that revitalization unfolded through a three-phase process-hardening, expansion, and alignment-that we term an incumbent-led industry revitalization. In the hardening phase, incumbents partnered with LSFs to professionalize livestreaming, but rigid templates reinforced traditional perceptions of pearls and yielded limited growth. During expansion, incumbents integrated livestreaming into their core businesses, using their deep industry expertise to deviate from LSFs' templates, introduce new designs, and broaden the meanings and uses of pearls. Meanwhile, entrants cultivated the perception of expertise through templated narratives and unverifiable claims, expanding but also destabilizing the value proposition. In the alignment phase, incumbents leveraged livestreaming's transparency to amplify their industry expertise and codify new evaluative standards, while entrants adapted by borrowing these standards and reinforcing incumbents' frameworks. We theorize expertise asymmetry enabled incumbents to harness entrants' technologies while maintaining control. The study contributes to research on industry evolution and technological change by explaining how incumbents can renew their industries' value propositions without being displaced by new entrants.

detail.abstract: The European Unionʼs AI Act embodies a dual regulatory approach, balancing product safety with the protection of fundamental rights. Initially focused on ensuring the safety of AI systems, the AI Act has increasingly broadened its scope to address the impact of AI on European values. Unlike traditional product regulations, which focus on physical harm, AI systems also introduce risks related to fundamental rights and democracy such as discrimination and surveillance. However, this dual approach presents regulatory complexities, as product safety regulations are based on technical compliance and standardised assessments, whereas the concerns related to fundamental rights and democracy are often context-dependent. This chapter examines the evolution of this dual nature in the AI Act and the challenges of coordinating these objectives within a coherent regulatory framework. It further explores potential aspects to reconcile safety and rights protection.

detail.title: To What Extent Does SHEIN’s Anticipated IPO Represent a Viable Long-Term Investment?
detail.abstract: This paper examines the potential long-term investment viability of fast-fashion retailer SHEIN in light of its pending IPO. We review SHEIN’s financial performance, business model, and market positioning to assess growth and compare it with major competitors (Zara, H&M, Temu). We also analyse crucial regulatory, legal and ethical/ESG risks that could affect SHEIN’s valuation and investor sentiment. Since the company is privately held, we are only able to use estimates that are reported from reputable sources (Reuters, FT, The Economic Times, Bloomberg, and SHEIN’s own ESG statement) and compare these with public peer data.  To delve further into investor response for SHEIN’s IPO, we have included models and matrixes highlighting various factors such as risks and speculation that investors are likely to construct on SHEIN’s future prospects. Some of the complications faced by SHEIN include new tariffs on imports, obscure administration (no official financial documentations)[5][6], and escalating ESG controversies such as labor conditions (child labor), carbon footprint, and growing government regulations[7][8].  Investors anticipate that SHEIN will need to lower its IPO price to satisfy market expectations (valuation reduced from ~$50B to ~$30B)[70]. We conclude that SHEIN’s IPO is appealing to risk tolerant investors seeking growth.However, for long-term investors it poses substantial risks due to the discussed factors above. The analysis is sourced by limited public data and the research compiled is just an educated estimate.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Modern Warfare: Strategic Stability and the Changing Global Balance of Power
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Modern Warfare: Strategic Stability and the Changing Global Balance of Power
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in international relations, fundamentally altering the conduct of warfare and reshaping the global balance of power. This paper argues that AI's strategic consequences are not determined by the technology itself but by the social, political, and cognitive contexts in which it is deployed. It examines how AI is transforming modern warfare across intelligence, command and control, and autonomous weapons, while also weaponising information and cognition through disinformation and influence operations. The paper further analyses how national approaches to defence AI, particularly those of the United States, China, Russia, India, and Ukraine, reflect divergent political systems and innovation ecosystems, influencing each state's capacity to integrate AI effectively. Critically, it highlights the risks of automation bias, algorithmic opacity, and compressed decision timelines, which threaten strategic stability and increase the likelihood of inadvertent escalation. The paper concludes that managing the intersection of AI and warfare demands robust international governance, clear norms for responsible military use, and renewed efforts to ensure meaningful human control over decisions of life and death.

detail.abstract: Emotion AI, technologies capable of detecting and responding to human emotions through facial expressions, voice tone, physiological signals, and textual cues, has emerged as a transformative force in digital marketing. By promising emotionally intelligent customer engagement, it blurs the line between personalization and manipulation. This article examines the ethical tensions surrounding the use of Emotion AI in marketing through a combined framework of the Influence Spectrum Model, Value Sensitive Design (VSD), and Stakeholder Responsibility Analysis. Using conceptual synthesis and comparative case analysis, the study draws upon secondary sources including Chavan et al. (2025), Fabiano (2025), and Arango-Kure and Garz (2025), as well as MorphCast's industry case studies, to explore how emotional profiling technologies operate at the intersection of empathy and exploitation. The paper argues that while Emotion AI enhances customer experience and marketing precision, it also risks covertly manipulating affective states, thereby undermining consumer autonomy and emotional privacy. The analysis situates these ethical challenges within the broader sociotechnical context of AI governance frameworks such as the EU AI Act and emerging digital ethics guidelines. Ultimately, the study proposes a pathway toward responsible affective marketing, emphasizing transparency, informed consent, and the embedding of moral values in algorithmic design. By reframing Emotion AI as not merely a marketing innovation but a moral instrument, this article contributes to the discourse on how empathy can coexist with integrity in the algorithmic marketplace, where understanding human feeling must not become a license to exploit it.

title: Macroeconomic Implications of FinTech in Nigeria

detail.title: Macroeconomic Implications of FinTech in Nigeria
detail.abstract: This study investigates the short-run macroeconomic implications of FinTech in Nigeria using quarterly time series data from 2009 to 2021. Anchored on the Schumpeterian creative destruction theory, new growth theory and neo classical growth theory, the study employs the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model to assess the impact of FinTech proxies such as ATM, Point of Sale (POS), and online (WEB) transactions on selected macroeconomic variables, including Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth, unemployment, financial sector performance, and interest rate. The short-run estimates show that ATM, POS, and WEB have a significant positive impact on unemployment (UNE). ATM and POS show a positive but insignificant impact on the financial sector's performance (FIEI). Conversely, WEB reveals a significantly negative impact on FIEI. The findings reveal a negative, insignificant relationship between ATM and interest rate (ILR), while POS, WEB (-1) and Inflation Rate (INFL) show a significant positive impact on interest rates. The results show that GDP growth can be significantly influenced by ATM innovations in Nigeria, however, POS and WEB show significantly negative impact on GDP growth. The study concludes that the impact of FinTech on selected economic variables depends on the type of innovation and the enabling infrastructure. Despite the growth of FinTech, transaction and lending costs remain high, with the potential to impede inclusion, real sector lending, and growth in the short term. Additionally, automation of services shows potential to impact employment growth. The study recommends promoting digital investment growth, enhancing skills, increasing internet penetration, and offering incentives for cost reduction to boost lending in the real sector, encourage inclusion, employment, and growth.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the background and personal life of Dr John Fullarton (esq), who graduated as a Doctor of Medicine from the University of Glasgow in 1800. Fullarton joined the British East India Company (BEIC) as a surgeon and settled in Calcutta, India, in 1802. He married there and joined the Bank of Bengal, which was a principal banking house in Calcutta, as a director in 1810 before resigning from the BEIC in 1812. He travelled extensively throughout India, Asia and Great Britain and died in London in 1849. This paper follows the key events of his life to give context to the man who wrote a seminal work on the regulation of currencies in the early Victorian era of the British Empire. This paper also clarifies several inaccuracies in previously published biographies and situates Fullarton's monetary views within their historical context. Though not an economist, Fullarton wrote extensively on his opinions of banking and its regulation, and On the Regulation of Currencies remains his major contribution. In this book, he argues that the value of banknotes issued by a bank must be supported by metallic coinage held in reserve to meet redemption on demand-a principle later known as the silver or gold standard. Despite being written in 1844, it remains a seminal criticism of Britain's banking system in the early 19 th century. His work provides valuable insight into the development of modern monetary economics, particularly the role bank regulation plays in governmental attempts to control the internal (inflation) and external (exchange rate) fluctuations in the value of national currencies.

detail.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Advancements on the Frequency and Severity of Flash Crashes in Financial Markets
detail.abstract: Flash crashes, sudden, severe market price dislocations followed by rapid recovery, reflect the growing influence of automation in financial trading. Since the 2010 event that erased nearly one trillion dollars in value within minutes, markets have become increasingly dependent on algorithmic and artificial intelligence (AI)driven systems. This narrative review examines how recent AI advancements, including machine-learning-based prediction and autonomous execution models, influence the frequency and severity of flash crashes. Evidence from empirical studies indicates that AI improves trading speed, liquidity, and efficiency but simultaneously amplifies systemic vulnerabilities through algorithmic clustering, herding effects, and opacity in decision-making. While regulatory mechanisms such as circuit breakers and the SEC's Limit-Up/Limit-Down Plan mitigate immediate volatility, persistent challenges remain in transparency, governance, and ethical oversight. The review concludes that AI's ultimate effect on financial stability depends on the balance between innovation and regulation, whether algorithmic intelligence becomes a stabilizing safeguard or a catalyst for new forms of market disruption.

detail.abstract: Fraud detection in financial transactions is a major and crucial problem that does not cease to exist, mainly because of the enormous imbalance in the datasets obtained and the very high requirement for an accurate distinction between legitimate and fraudulent activities. In the following study, we assess the performance of three common machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, for the detection of fraud, using a real-data set of transactions (284807 of which only 0.173% are labelled as fraudulent). The models were thoroughly evaluated with respect to critical metrics of performance including the precision, recall, F1-score and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) to try to understand which of the models may be appropriate for dealing with class imbalance and false positives. Of the analyzed models, Random Forest was the best, with AUC being equal to 0.98, being superior to Logistic Regression (AUC = 0.97) and equal to Gradient Boosting (AUC = 0.98), while enabling more superior recall (0.88) and precision (0.44). This implies a higher capacity of detecting fraud cases without compromising the rate of false alarm too much. Feature importance analysis further noted that V14, V10, and V4 features were most predictive and most responsible for model classifying accuracy. Furthermore, calibration analysis revealed that Random Forest was the most reliable in estimating probabilities, outputs closely conformed to the ideal calibration curve implicating better reliability in practical applications. These findings suggest the effectiveness of the ensemble machine learning models especially Random Forest in promoting the efficacy of fraud detection systems. The study supports future research on real-time deployment and integration with deep learning methods to enhance the strength of fraud detection in the constantly changing financial spaces.

detail.abstract: We examine what is widely considered to be one of the strongest channels of monetary policy transmission into household spending-the effect of changes in mortgage payments when mortgage rates are linked to the short-term policy rate. Using bank transactions data from Australia, we analyze a cumulative 425 basis point increase in the central bank policy rate, which caused mortgage repayments for homeowners with adjustable-rate mortgages to increase by $13,800. We find little change in the spending of adjustable-rate mortgagors relative to fixedrate mortgagors. This is because adjustable-rate mortgages come with redraw facilities that make mortgages liquid, and households had large excess buffers due to pandemic-era transfer programs and restrictions on spending. Our findings demonstrate that the direct effects of a monetary policy tightening on household spending need not be large.

detail.abstract: Urgent global threats like climate change demand large-scale collective action, yet collective action often fails-even if people in general are well-intentioned. Standard models struggle to explain this fragility because they overlook a critical feature of realworld groups: heterogeneity. People differ in their responses as they have different sensitivities. In this study, we develop a theory-driven, empirically grounded agentbased model (ABM) to examine how differences in individuals' sensitivities to social norms and environmental risk shape collective outcomes. We formalize four empirically informed decision-making types and show that success or failure of collective action hinges not on average behavior, but on population composition and the interactions between behavioral types. Our model reproduces key empirical patterns and outperforms simpler alternatives that assume homogeneity or isolate individual mechanisms. Crucially, we find that targeting interventions at already cooperative individuals (rather than those contributing the least) can produce stronger and more lasting effects, due to positive social norm spillovers on others. These findings reframe collective action under risk as a problem of strategic composition, offering new insights for the design of behavioral interventions: identifying and engaging the right subgroups can be more effective than trying to reach everyone equally.

detail.abstract: This study endeavors to reveal the macroeconomic determinants influencing remittance inflows to Bangladesh, a country heavily dependent on the remittance income for macroeconomic stability and development. Based on the annual data ranging from 1980-2023, the paper employs Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model for cointegration to determine both short-run and long-run associations between remittance growth and major macroeconomic variables including GDP growth, inflation, interest rate differentials, exchange rate fluctuations, unemployment in host countries and global oil prices.  The study reveals that remittance growth is counter-cyclical to the GDP growth of Bangladesh and pro-cyclical with respect to the economic conditions of host countries while inflation and unemployment in host economies demonstrate strong positive impacts. These patterns of behavior suggest altruistic motives dominate remittance behavior particularly in economic distress in home country and inflationary pressure abroad. This paper confirms the existence of long-run cointegration among the variables and highlights the rapid short-run responsiveness of remittance growth due to host-country labor market shocks. The diagnostic tests validate the model’s robustness, normality and stability. The negative sign of error correction term (ECT) suggests adjustment of the variables toward long-run equilibrium but value more than 1 indicates a problem which may have arisen from using less frequency time series data. Future research should explore the association of remittance inflows with macroeconomic determinants using high frequency data and incorporating non-linearities in the model.

detail.abstract: How does present bias shape economic growth, the creation of ideas, natural resource extraction, and pollution? We develop an endogenous growth model with exhaustible resources and pollution, where households have tendencies to procrastinate. Relative to exponential discounting, which is time-consistent, outcomes depend on an EIS threshold. detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Symbiotic Civilization framework—a post-anthropocentric paradigm integrating planetary cognition, Indigenous knowledge, and systems science to operationalize regenerative intelligence at the planetary scale. Synthesizing insights from over two hundred peer-reviewed studies across ecology, economics, and cognitive science, the study merges Indigenous ecological epistemologies (Kimmerer, 2013; Nelson & Shilling, 2018) with research in planetary cognition (Frank et al., 2022; Haqq-Misra et al., 2024) and post-growth economics (Hickel, 2020; Raworth, 2018). It identifies twelve modes of Symbiotic Design across material, adaptive, and regenerative domains. These modes are translated into measurable indices—the Material Regeneration Index (MRI), Adaptive Intelligence Index (AII), and Relational Coherence Score (RCS)—which together form the composite Planetary Coherence Index (PCI), quantifying civilization’s alignment with Earth’s autopoietic intelligence. Three testable hypotheses link biogenic design principles, pluriversal governance models, and autopoietic feedback systems with measurable improvements in resilience and ecological balance. Advancing beyond regeneration toward coherence and, ultimately, symbiosis, the framework positions civilization as a distributed organ of Earth’s cognitive metabolism and establishes a pathway toward a Planetary Symbiosis Index (PSI)—a next-generation metric of planetary participation and mutual flourishing. This is the first framework to quantify civilization’s contribution to planetary cognition through measurable indices of material, adaptive, and relational coherence.

detail.title: Spatio-Temporal Shifts in War Terminology
detail.abstract: One of the reasons for arguments is the objective definition of words. A deeper problem arises when people define words differently across space and time, leading to significant discursive tensions. For example, the word "terrorist" demonstrates a drastic shift in meaning over time. During the French Revolution in the late 18th century, the term was used to describe state agents who used violence to maintain order and control. By the 19th century, the term began to refer to non-state actors using violence against governments. In the modern era, especially after the events of 9/11, "terrorist" refers almost exclusively to non-state actors targeting civilians. Similarly, the term "coloniser" is far from neutral: from a Palestinian standpoint, colonisation is rooted in the post-1967 occupation of the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and Gaza, whereas other framings project legitimacy backwards to earlier periods, selectively invoking history to define who 'first' belongs. Meanwhile, others, especially those supporting Israel, frame their perspective through a much earlier historical lens, dating back to around 1200 BCE to 70 CE, when ancient Jewish kingdoms such as Israel and Judah existed in the land historically known as Canaan or Judea. In this context, the term "return" is used instead of "colonisation," reflecting a belief in an ancestral right to the land. By placing the same conflict within different time frames, both sides use historical narratives to validate their claims. This illustrates how the use of language involves various dimensions of time and space, generating semantic and political conflict. This paper analyses how the shifting definitions of terms, along with their manipulation and contestation, contribute to misunderstandings, bias, and politicised narratives in media representations of wars.

Spanish Abstract: Esta investigación revisa las estrategias de aprendizaje, tradicionalmente empleadas en las escuelas, facultades o departamentos para la enseñanza de los negocios o la administración de empresas, identificando aquellos cambios que pudieran garantizar una formación virtuosa de su alumnado acorde con las realidades regionales y con las posibilidades de incidir en la ruralidad. El propósito fundamental consiste en descubrir las formas como la comunidad estudiantil de licenciatura puede incidir rural y socialmente dejando de lado, por un momento, la idea de las finalidades lucrativas, para concentrarse en las necesidades de las comunidades agropecuarias. Para ello, y con ocasión de una serie de visitas del estudiantado de siete licenciaturas relacionadas con los negocios, a tres localidades poblanas, se explora mediante cuestionario aquellos rasgos de carácter que pudieran reforzarse y asimilarse en sus procesos formativos. Se encontró, por un lado, potencial y disposición del alumnado para la apropiación de rasgos tendientes a la búsqueda del bien común, y por otro, la urgente necesidad de ajustar los contenidos de algunas asignaturas. Hay que decirlo, entre la población estudiada se percibieron rasgos de arrogancia, soberbia y egoísmo, que a todas luces constituyen el opuesto de virtudes como humildad, altruismo e interés común. Y es que persiste, en la población estudiantil de negocios, la idea de que todas las actividades en aula y fuera de ella, tienen que ver con la licenciatura estudiada y por tanto, las aproximaciones a la población vulnerable no son de su competencia. English Abstract: This research reviews the learning strategies traditionally used at schools, faculties or departments to teach either business or administration. We identify those changes that could contribute to the virtuous formation of their students according to regional realities and with possibilities to impact on rurality. The main purpose is discovering those ways undergraduate students could impact rurally and socially, putting aside for a moment, the idea of lucrative purposes, and instead of that focalize the agricultural community’s needs. To achieve this and framed in a set of students’ visits to three Puebla rural locations we applied a questionary about main virtues to teach and to assimilate in their formative processes. Findings show, first, that there is a potential and will of students to acquire character traits tending to the common good, and second, it is urgent to adjust some subjects’ contents. It is important to recognize that some students exhibited some traits of hubris, arrogance and selfishness, that obviously are the opposite of virtues such as humbleness, altruism and common wellbeing. This is because in the student community there is a belief that all activities both in the classroom and extracurricular activities must be related to their undergraduate program, so all kinds of approaching activities to the vulnerable population are not their responsibility.

detail.abstract: This research examines the impact of chief executive officer (CEO) overconfidence on firms’ trademarking activities reflected in new trademark registrations. The authors hypothesize that firms with overconfident CEOs register a higher number of new trademarks. The positive relation strengthens in firms in advertising-dependent industries, firms facing more intensive product market competition, or in industries with higher business uncertainties, and firms led by more capable CEOs. Moreover, firms led by overconfident CEOs are more likely to pursue trademarks in new product categories and to adopt distinctive new brand names, reflecting a preference for higher-risk trademarking strategies. Trademarks registered by firms led by overconfident CEOs demonstrate higher brand impacts and greater market value. Using a sample of S&P 1500 firms from 1993 to 2015, the authors find evidence supporting their hypotheses. The authors also explore changes in firms’ trademarking activities around exogenous CEO turnovers and find evidence consistent with their conjecture. These findings uncover the role of executives’ personal traits in influencing how firms leverage trademarks to support product innovation and brand development, offering a novel pathway through which leaders contribute to firm value.

detail.abstract: We consider Hamiltonian diagnostics built on the empirical first four moments of a financial return distribution, using mean, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis as phase-space coordinates. A common (and seductive) implementation scales all coordinates by recent empirical dispersion to produce a "dimensionless" chart. We show this "double-normalisation" is inappropriate for already-normalised shape descriptors (skewness and kurtosis). It induces spurious curvature in the potential energy of an otherwise linear Hamiltonian, leading to explosive energies in quiet windows. We formalise the pathology, provide a principled construction that treats dimensional and dimensionless coordinates differently, and demonstrate empirically that the corrected model yields stable, interpretable energy partitions that cleanly distinguish trend from trap regimes. This methodological note addresses a gap at the intersection of Hamiltonian moment hierarchies (typically applied to raw moments in plasma physics) and statistical diagnostics (which employ pre-normalized shape descriptors).

detail.abstract:
This Article presents the Michigan Youth Dignity in Medicine Act, a state-level legislative model designed to restore medical parity for transgender minors in Michigan. Under the state’s civil rights law (ELCRA), public accommodations — including hospitals — may not discriminate on the basis of gender identity. Yet several Michigan hospital systems have suspended gender-affirming care for minors while continuing to use the exact same puberty blockers, hormone therapies, and clinical protocols for cisgender minors with other medical indications. This selective denial is not medically grounded; it is an identity-based exclusion that violates both established clinical standards and the Constitution’s core commitment to bodily autonomy.

The Act responds by requiring parity: if a medical treatment is considered safe, accepted, and medically necessary for cisgender youth, it must be equally available to transgender youth under the same clinical criteria. This is not the creation of new rights or special access — it is the enforcement of existing legal and medical standards. In terms of constitutional physiology, the bill corrects a failure of recognition: when the state treats one group as real patients and another as exceptions, it triggers systemic instability and predictable harm, including sharply elevated rates of depression and suicidality among youth denied care.

The Act is narrowly tailored, evidence-based, and reversible through an autophagic wind-down mechanism if parity is no longer necessary. It protects clinical judgment, family autonomy, and the integrity of medical institutions, while reaffirming the principle that care is how a Republic acknowledges the humanity of its people. The legislation is offered as a model for other states seeking durable, non-punitive, constitutional solutions that restore homeostasis rather than escalate harm.

detail.abstract:
The Venezuela Dignity Preservation Act (Phase I) responds to ongoing humanitarian emergency conditions affecting over 14 million Venezuelans, where collapse of health, food, and civil infrastructure prevents safe return. Venezuelan Temporary Protected Status (TPS) recipients in the United States have demonstrated exceptionally high compliance rates (91–99%), strong labor participation, and over $2.8 billion in annual economic contributions. Allowing TPS to expire under these conditions would constitute systemic misrecognition: the State would treat an integrated, law-abiding population as a threat, triggering an autoimmune reflex within the civic body.

This Act provides an 18-month automatic TPS extension and establishes renewable parole-in-place to maintain family unity, community stability, and work authorization, without expanding detention or enforcement authority. The Act is narrowly tailored, operates within existing INA §244 and parole frameworks, and includes an autophagic wind-down clause that tapers protections once humanitarian conditions stabilize and reactivates them if harm returns.

This legislation restores constitutional homeostasis by ensuring defense cools into care, maintaining dignity as a stabilizing force in the Republic.

detail.title: Validation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Mapping Flood Inundation and Slum Expansion in East African Cities
detail.abstract: In Sub-Saharan Africa, approximately 50% of the urban population resides in slums. Yet studies examining the spatiotemporal development and flood vulnerability of slums remain scarce in East African cities. This study aims to (i) analyse spatial-temporal dynamics in the Kibera (Kenya) and Katanga (Uganda) slums, Compared to Bannyahe, a former slum in Rwanda whose residents were successfully relocated to the Busanza model village, and (ii) to quantitatively assess flood exposure across various land use/land cover (LULC) categories and exposed population. We applied the Random Forest (RF) Algorithm classification to Landsat 7,8 and 9 (2012–2024) for LULC mapping, alongside Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)-based flood detection using Sentinel-1. The model was trained with a 70% training and 30% testing split and evaluated via confusion matrices and Kappa, achieving 92.75% accuracy for RF and 89% for SAR. The results show (1) that built-up areas increased significantly in Kibera (86.67%) and Katanga (77.52%) slums. In Bannyahe experienced a decline of 32.22% after 2021, which is attributed to the successful relocation to Busanza model village. (2) An overlay analysis of flood exposure across LULC categories during all flood events revealed total flooded areas of 112.50 hectares in Kibera slum and 7.20 hectares in Katanga slum. Population estimates indicate that more than 45,000 residents were exposed in Kibera. Importantly, our algorithms produce flood maps over affected areas and estimate exposed populations within minutes, making them easily applicable to other regions. This study recommends a similar resettlement approach adopted in Bannyahe.

title: The cost of mistakes and entrepreneurial strategy formation
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Management

detail.title: The cost of mistakes and entrepreneurial strategy formation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Columbia Business School Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: Columbia Business School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Entrepreneurs form strategy under high uncertainty, often relying on either reasoning-oriented approaches that prioritize analysis ahead of decisions or action-oriented approaches that emphasize learning through execution. Yet when and why entrepreneurs lean toward one approach over the other remains under-examined. This study theorizes that entrepreneurs' perceived cost of mistakes shapes this choice. When entrepreneurs perceive mistakes to be costlier, they place greater value on accuracy—minimizing deviations from expected outcomes—which reasoning-oriented approaches tend to provide. Action-oriented approaches, in contrast, may sacrifice such accuracy to gain speed, both in executing decisions and in discovering more optimal strategies. Using interviews covering more than 1,200 strategic choices made by scaling software startups around the world and large language models (LLMs), the study finds that a higher perceived cost of mistakes is associated with 6% greater use of reasoning-oriented approaches and 11% lower use of action-oriented approaches. Entrepreneurs in more resource-constrained environments, facing higher-commitment organizational decisions, and with a prevention orientation perceive mistakes as costlier. A supplementary experiment that exogenously varies the cost of mistakes around a key scaling decision yields consistent results. Together, the findings suggest that the cost of mistakes is an important mechanism shaping how entrepreneurs form strategy.

title: The Alwadhi Power-Law of Diamond Pricing: A Universal Mathematical Framework for Gemstone Valuation
affiliations: Maison Alwadhi ®

detail.title: The Alwadhi Power-Law of Diamond Pricing: A Universal Mathematical Framework for Gemstone Valuation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Maison Alwadhi, an institution engaged in diamond research and valuation methodologies. The author may hold financial interests in potential applications of the model. No external funding influenced the theoretical development or empirical validation of this work.
declarations.funderStatement: This work is entirely self-funded. No institutional, governmental, or commercial funding was provided.

detail.abstract: We establish the first universal mathematical law for diamond pricing, addressing a fundamental gap in economic theory that has persisted since the formalization of commodity markets. The Alwadhi Power-Law states that diamond price scales with carat weight according to P = B • W α • C s • M q , where the critical exponent α = 1.725 ± 0.012 emerges from the intersection of geological scarcity distributions, fractal formation processes, and market equilibrium dynamics. Through analysis of 1.2 million transaction records across global markets (2019-2024) and rigorous theoretical derivation from first principles, we demonstrate that this law represents a fundamental economic relationship analogous to gravity in physics or allometric scaling in biology. The power-law exponent sits precisely at the boundary between normal market behavior (α < 2) and bubble dynamics (α > 2), suggesting an efficient market equilibrium shaped by natural constraints. Empirical validation yields R 2 = 0.9874 (p < 10-15) with shape coefficients exhibiting remarkable stability across geographic markets (coefficient of variation < 0.03). The law's mathematical structure enables closed-form solutions for derivative pricing, portfolio optimization, and risk assessment while maintaining computational efficiency three orders of magnitude superior to machine learning alternatives. This work not only provides the diamond industry with its first scientific pricing framework but also contributes to the broader understanding of power laws in economic systems, demonstrating how physical constraints and market forces combine to produce universal scaling relationships in commodity valuation.

publicationDetails.detailsText: MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics Research Paper No. 2025/034

detail.abstract: We introduce BMSSPy, the first open-source Python package faithfully implementing the Bounded Multi-Source Shortest Path (BMSSP) algorithm, recently proposed as a breakthrough beyond Dijkstra's sorting barrier for single-source shortest paths. BMSSPy translates theoretical advances into practice: it preserves the algorithm's asymptotic performance guarantees while returning both distance labels and route predecessors. Our implementation resolves core ambiguities in pivot selection, tight-edge forest construction, and frontier management that prior work left open for practitioners. We engineer BMSSPy to handle graphs with non-unique path lengths, structural irregularities, unreachable vertices, and highly variable node degrees, ensuring function and robust performance on real data. Extensive experiments on grid and geospatial networks demonstrate that BMSSPy delivers competitive performance. For instance, on a graph with 200,000 nodes and 1.56 million edges, BMSSP runs 1.7× faster than NetworkX's Dijkstra and up to 3.5× faster than igraph's, although the highly optimized SCGraph Modified Dijkstra still achieves the best performance. BMSSP proves practical and efficient in practice, despite the remaining gap between theory and system-level performance. BMSSPy, with full documentation and reproducibility scripts, is released to support future research and development in shortest-path algorithms.

title: Evaluating Accuracy of Ethiopian Building Code's Prediction for flexure of RC Beam Using Neural Networks
affiliations: Aksum University

detail.title: Evaluating Accuracy of Ethiopian Building Code's Prediction for flexure of RC Beam Using Neural Networks
detail.abstract: Abstract:  The Ethiopian building code standard is a theoretically based design process that was created to address restrictions, however it is not fully consistent with fundamental material attributes. The goal of this research was to evaluate the accuracy of Ethiopian building code techniques for the design of simply supported RC beams in order to perform flexural capacity tests. The design prediction of the flexural capacity of a simply supported RC beam of the compulsory Ethiopian standard (CES-2015) was compared to available experimental prediction, compressive-force path method based on assumption, different from code adapted, and artificial neural networks that were calibrated based on the available test result. This research shows that artificial neural network predictions of the flexural capacity of RC beams are very close to the experimental flexural capacity of RC beams. In addition, while the compressive force-path method is closer to the experimental than the code, it is not as effective as ANNs. When compared to other approaches, the CES-2015 method was a poor predictor of the RC beam's flexural capacity. As a result, using the input-based systematic technique and the compressive–force path method as RC structure design methods reduces the incompatibility between the CES-2015 methodologies and fundamental concrete material properties. The findings are expected to aid structural engineers who work on high-rise building analysis and design.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how international trade shocks transmit through domestic supply chains, shaping local economic vulnerabilities. Using detailed firm-to-firm domestic and foreign transaction data, we quantify the direct and indirect exposure of Italian labor markets to two major sources of external risk: imports from China and exports to the United States. We quantify the importance of firms’ domestic and foreign linkages for overall exposure and highlight the critical role of wholesalers and top trading firms within the domestic network in shaping tails risks. Pronounced local disparities in exposure reveal that aggregate trade statistics conceal substantial and uneven regional vulnerabilities.

detail.abstract: This study constructs the Egypt Patriarchy Index (EPI), drawing on methodologies developed by Gruber and Szołtysek (2016) and expanded by Singh et al. (2022). The EPI incorporates five key dimensions: male domination, generational domination, patrilocality, son preference, and socioeconomic domination. Utilizing data from five rounds of the Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) conducted in Egypt from 1995 to 2014, this index offers comprehensive insights into patriarchal structures at both national and sub-national levels. The study reveals persistent and deeply entrenched patriarchy in Egypt, with only minor fluctuations over two decades. The reliability and validity of the EPI are confirmed through high Cronbach's Alpha values and a strong correlation with the Gender Inequality Index (GII), demonstrating that higher levels of patriarchy correspond to greater gender inequality. These findings highlight significant regional variations in patriarchy across Egyptian governorates and underscore the necessity for region-specific gender equality interventions. The EPI provides a valuable tool for assessing and addressing patriarchal norms, contributing to the broader discourse on gender inequality in Egypt and similar socio-cultural contexts.

title: Retailing Technology: Innovations and Impact on Consumer Experience
affiliations: University of Johannesburg

detail.title: Retailing Technology: Innovations and Impact on Consumer Experience
detail.abstract: Strong governance, con guration management, and compliance frameworks are critical to prevent scope drift, misalignment, and traceability challenges that frequently undermine the success of retail technology projects. Retail digitalization-driven by arti cial intelligence (AI), augmented reality (AR), Internet of Things (IoT), and data governance systems-has rede ned how consumer experience (CX), operational control, and innovation are managed in modern retail ecosystems. This systematic review evaluates the evolution, application, and governance of retail technologies from 2015 to 2025, focusing on their effects on consumer engagement, satisfaction, and loyalty, as well as the organizational mechanisms that ensure their sustainable integration. Following the PRISMA framework, a total of 267 studies were initially identi ed from Scopus (41%), Web of Science (29%), and Google Scholar (30%). After screening and eligibility assessment, 56 peer-reviewed studies met inclusion criteria based on methodological rigor, relevance to retail technology governance, and CX outcomes. Research activity exhibited three phases—emergence (2015–2017, 10.7%), growth (2018–2021, 38.3%), and maturity (2022–2025, 50.0%)—reflecting an evolution from conceptual frameworks to data-driven governance models. Geographically, the literature is dominated by European (46.0%) and Asia-Pacific (35.7%) contributions, shaped by strong regulatory and digital innovation policies. Technological clusters reveal an emphasis on AI and automation (17.9%), AR/VR immersive systems (17.9%), IoT and smart retail infrastructures (14.3%), and computer vision (14.3%), underscoring the growing interdependence between intelligence, automation, and experience design. Thematically, over 60% of studies center on process and service innovation, while 51.8% of applied research focuses on in-store retail transformation, highlighting the ongoing digitalization of physical retail environments. Consumer outcomes are dominated by convenience and accessibility (41.1%) and engagement and experience (28.6%), followed by satisfaction, trust, and personalization dimensions. Organizationally, most studies emphasize operational efficiency (26.8%) and automation-driven optimization (12.5%), while governance challenges cluster around privacy and ethical concerns (19.6%), integration complexity (18.9%), and adoption barriers (17.8%). Emerging governance criteria highlight user-centered design (21.4%), data ethics and transparency (20.5%), and ethical AI integration (18.9%), reflecting a growing maturity in balancing innovation with accountability. Finally, innovation trends point toward AI and automation (20.9%), immersive retail experiences (17.9%), and IoT-edge distributed commerce (16.1%), signaling a shift toward intelligent, self-regulating, and sustainability-oriented retail ecosystems. Retail technology innovation has advanced from fragmented, tool-based applications to integrated, governance-oriented frameworks that align operational performance with consumer experience. However, gaps persist in system interoperability, cost-efficiency, and empirical evaluation of governance effectiveness. To strengthen adoption and long-term impact, the study recommends targeted capacity-building, affordable integration solutions, and cross-sector partnerships between vendors and retailers. Future research should prioritize longitudinal and evidence-based evaluation of governance mechanisms to determine how specific design and policy strategies influence measurable consumer and organizational outcomes.

detail.abstract: This paper discusses the attributes and design of alternative mitigation instruments for the industrial sector, their competitiveness and emissions leakage impacts, and supplementary measures to address these effects. detail.abstract: This paper develops and analyses the steady-state properties and stability conditions of an Export-Led Cumulative (ELCC) Causation model that integrates elements from new developmentalism and evolutionary-Schumpeterian growth theories. The standard ELCC model proposed by Dixon and Thirlwall (1975) suggests that the growth rate of exports, which drives economic development, depends on the rate of change of the exchange rate and the growth rate of the world´s income. Therefore, it neglects the roles of the exchange rate level, manufacturing structure, and technological gap. This study advances the theoretical foundation by introducing five key novelties: (i) export growth as a function of the real exchange rate level via a dynamic replicator mechanism, following Boggio and Barbieri (2017); (ii) an employment-dependent Kaldor-Verdoorn coefficient, as in Setterfield (2006), in which this paper explicit the driving role of the manufacturing shares; (iii) a stratification mechanism where export income elasticity adjusts to output growth differentials (Dávila-Fernández et al., 2018); finally, (iv) an endogenous evolution of manufacturing shares driven by both price and non-price competitiveness.

detail.abstract: Background: U.S. federal outlays reached 23.3% of GDP ($7.0 trillion) in FY2025 [Congressional Budget Office, 2025]. Objective: Quantify the scale and structural context of means-tested redistribution as the core pillar of a hypothesized four-pillar extraction framework (redistribution, defense, addiction, climate-driven asset repricing), with extensions to a full ∼$5.2 trillion aggregation. Methods: Data fusion from CBO (FY2025 baseline), IRS SOI (2024), DOJ/FBI UCR (2025 quarterly), Swiss Re sigma (2025), OECD SOCR (2025), FEMA Risk Rating 2.0 (2025), CDC/White House (2025), and Urban Institute (2025). Full framework: ∼$5.2 trillion, including $1.5-4 trillion coastal propertyvalue transfer by 2040 (FEMA/Swiss Re). Conclusion: The configuration is consistent with a high-extraction equilibrium supported by institutional incentives; illustrative off-ramps draw from Utah JRI (∼40% recidivism reduction) and Florida DCF OPBI Fraud Recovery (∼50% of investigated overpayments).

title: Corporate Governance by Workers
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and University of Texas at Dallas - School of Management - Department of Finance & Managerial Economics

detail.title: Corporate Governance by Workers
detail.abstract: We study how workers' private information about managerial performance shapes equity financing and compensation structures. We develop a simple moral-hazard model in which a manager exerts unobservable effort and workers observe that effort before deciding whether to stay with the firm. When workers are compensated partly in equity, their decision to quit following low managerial effort disciplines the manager, generating internal corporate governance. This mechanism introduces a novel link between equity financing and labor contracting: worker equity both incentivizes managerial effort and exerts downward pressure on wages, since underpayment is necessary for the manager to lose surplus when workers leave. In equilibrium, workers are optimally paid entirely in equity and below the monopsony-optimal compensation level, trading off profit extraction against the strength of managerial incentives. The model proposes a new governance mechanism by worker departure and provides a new explanation for the prevalence of worker equity compensation.

detail.title: Tourism Development and Economic Scale: Assessing the Relationship between Tourism Growth and the Size of National Economies
detail.abstract: This paper explores how the scale of an economy influences the patterns, benefits, and challenges of tourism development. By comparing small and large economies, the study examines how differences in resource capacity, institutional structure, and market openness affect the sustainability of tourism-led growth. Drawing on international evidence and case studies, the analysis highlights that small economies often depend more heavily on tourism revenues, which can stimulate employment and foreign exchange but also increase vulnerability to external shocks. In contrast, larger economies tend to integrate tourism within more diversified development strategies, where its contribution to GDP and employment is significant but less dominant. The paper argues that the effectiveness of tourism as a driver of development depends not solely on economic size, but on governance quality, environmental management, and social inclusiveness. These comparative insights provide guidance for designing balanced, sustainable tourism policies across diverse national contexts.

title: Determinants of Household’s Participation in Urban Vegetable Production in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Mixed Research Approach
affiliations: Gambella University, Haramaya University, Haramaya University and Bahir Dar University

detail.title: Determinants of Household’s Participation in Urban Vegetable Production in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: A Mixed Research Approach
detail.abstract: Urban agriculture is vital for alleviating food insecurity and promoting urban living, leading to more sustainable and resilient communities. Despite its importance, a household’s participation in it in Addis Ababa remains low due to various demographic, socioeconomic, and institutional factors. Therefore, this study seeks to determine the factors that affect household participation in urban vegetable production in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The multi-stage sampling method was used to select the samples. The sample size was 400 households. Both quantitative and qualitative data types were used. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used to summarize and compare household characteristics. The probit model was used to analyze the factors influencing a household’s decision to participate using the R (V.4.5.4) tool. Thematic analysis was applied to analyze qualitative data using the NVivo (V.12) tool. The findings indicate that factors such as gender, household size, water, land, improved seed, extension, and attitude positively influenced households' participation in urban vegetable production, whereas age and knowledge negatively affected participation. Moreover, mixed effects were observed for marital status, education, occupation, and tenure systems. Generally, marital status, water, land, improved seed, training, extension, and attitude significantly and positively influence household participation.  Collectively, these findings provide strong implications for practice, theory, and policy. Additionally, the findings of the study will assist policymakers, program designers, and project managers in developing effective interventions that encourage households’ participation to enhance food security and sustainable livelihoods, especially for low-income urban households. The findings also serve as a source of information for researchers.

title: What are we Measuring? Measurement and Aggregation Issues in Economics, with an Application to Climate Risks
affiliations: and University of Oxford

detail.title: What are we Measuring? Measurement and Aggregation Issues in Economics, with an Application to Climate Risks
detail.abstract: This paper reviews the twin challenges of measurement and aggregation in economics and the natural sciences, with climate risk as a guiding example. It synthesises a broad range of theoretical and empirical perspectives, tracing ideas from early systems theory to modern macroeconomic debates, and compares the approaches of economics, complexity science, and climate science to the micro-macro aggregation problem. Several key conceptual tensions are highlighted-most notably the "micro-macro gap"-and the limitations of traditional models when confronted with heterogeneity, deep uncertainty, and non-linear feedbacks are demonstrated, especially in the climate-risk context. It also reviews emerging methodologies and proposes integrated frameworks to combine micro-level detail with macro-level consistency. Finally, the paper outlines a roadmap for future research and policy, advocating interdisciplinary collaboration, improved data infrastructure, and adaptive modelling strategies to better capture climate change.

title: Utilizing Foreign Currency-Denominated Collaterals for Naira Loans and the Position of the Central Bank of Nigeria
