detail.title: Intraseasonal Variations in Time Use, Food Security, and Health Outcomes among Women in Rural Malawi ✻
detail.abstract: The sequential nature of agriculture poses significant challenges to rural women in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in managing health and balancing farm and domestic work across different periods of the agricultural cycle. Despite its importance, empirical evidence on these intraseasonal dynamics remains limited. This study investigates intraseasonal variations in time use, food security, and anthropometric outcomes among female caregivers in 300 farm households in rural Malawi, using panel data collected at four points during the 2022/2023 agricultural season. Results show that women's work hours increase during the lean period, reducing leisure time. Food insecurity also worsens during this period, contributing to declines in women's nutritional status, particularly as measured by mid-upper arm circumference. Fluctuations in body weight further suggest community-wide structural dynamics within the agricultural season beyond individual health, labor supply, and household food insecurity. Overall, the findings underscore the need for policies that account for within-season variation-particularly the pre-harvest hunger period-to improve food security, nutritional outcomes, and, ultimately, women's welfare in rural Malawi.

detail.abstract: Countries routinely participate in intergovernmental forums such as the G7, G20, BRICS, and MIKTA. These informal institutions—unlike formal bodies such as the EU and WTO—lack permanent administrative structures, operate through rotating presidencies, and do not issue legally binding commitments. Although often overlooked as drivers of global trade, their formation and evolution embody underlying structural shifts in the world economy. Using data for over 200 countries spanning 1994-2023, this study introduces informal institutions as a distinct determinant of trade within the gravity framework. We find that BRICS exerts trade-facilitating effects comparable to those of formal agreements such as regional trade agreements and WTO accession. This highlights a novel channel of international integration beyond legal commitments.

detail.abstract: Rainwater harvesting (RWH) has become a long-term way to deal with water shortages and encourage better water use. This study examines recent technological innovations in rainwater harvesting systems, emphasising their design, implementation, and optimisation. Smart sensors for real-time monitoring, automatic filtration systems to make sure the water is clean, and interaction with IoT platforms for data-driven administration are some of the most important new ideas. The research assesses the influence of these technologies on system efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and environmental advantages. The study uses case studies and comparative research to show how technology can make rainwater harvesting more scalable and reliable, making it a good choice for both urban and rural water supply. The results show that combining technology with other methods could help spread sustainable water conservation techniques over the world.

detail.abstract: The Prudential Regulation has raised the issue of estimation errors due to Internal Rating Based (IRB) estimation process that may produce underestimation of the risk measures. In the context of credit risk, lower bounds (i.e. floors) for the estimated parameters are introduced to limit the impact of such possible underestimation. These floors are heuristically justified by the difficulties to estimate the parameters when the default event becomes rare, as in the case of Low Default Probability Portfolios (LDP). In this paper, on the basis of a standard Asymptotic Single Risk Factor (ASRF) model, and by means of Monte Carlo simulations, we provide a robust justification to PD floors, and a framework for their calibration. Our results give hints that the introduction of a floor can indeed mitigate the possibility that the risk measures become less reliable.

title: Internalizing Spatial-Dynamic Externalities: Endemic Disease in Chilean Aquaculture
affiliations: University of Florida, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of California, Davis and University of California

detail.title: Internalizing Spatial-Dynamic Externalities: Endemic Disease in Chilean Aquaculture
detail.abstract: Spatial-dynamic externalities are pervasive in environmental and resource systems, yet the appropriate spatial scale of policies remains poorly understood and difficult to evaluate. We study this problem in Chile's salmon aquaculture industry, where policymakers implemented a spatial management program to limit the transmission of infectious diseases. Using industry-wide panel data on veterinary outcomes and antimicrobial use, we test whether this spatially-explicit policy effectively contains pathogens by measuring spillovers across management boundaries. Exploiting policy-induced exogenous variation in pathogen prevalence, we find little evidence of disease spillover between management units and no response in antimicrobial use to pathogen pressure in neighboring units. These results suggest that Chile's spatial management policy protects against the spread of transmissible disease from one unit to another, offering rare empirical evidence on the spatial scale of management internalizing spatial-dynamic externalities.

title: Mathematical Foundations of Explainability: A Unified Theory Across Dimensions and Domains
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: Mathematical Foundations of Explainability: A Unified Theory Across Dimensions and Domains
detail.abstract: We develop a comprehensive mathematical theory of explainability that unifies fundamental limitations with domain-specific analyses. This work establishes that explainability is not a monolithic problem but varies fundamentally across three axes: (1) dimensionality-from tractable low-dimensional problems to intractable high-dimensional spaces; (2) domain structure-the mathematical properties of input/output spaces and loss functions; and (3) model architecture-from interpretable linear models to opaque deep networks with superposition. We prove fundamental impossibility results including: computational intractability of exact attribution (Theorem 2.3: Ω(2 d) complexity via formal reduction), nonuniqueness due to the Rashomon effect (Theorem 3.1), superposition-induced polysemanticity (Theorem 3.5: m/n → ∞ makes monosemantic neurons vanish with probability O(n/m), proven via sparse coding capacity arguments), and universal trade-offs between fidelity, stability, and comprehensibility (Theorem 10.1). Through rigorous domain-specific analysis of large language models, regression, classification, computer vision, reinforcement learning, time series, and financial models, we demonstrate how these limitations manifest differently across applications. Our dimensional heterogeneity analysis (Section 8) reveals that effective dimensionality-not ambient dimensionality-determines tractability, with exact methods feasible for d eff ≤ 20, approximations for 20 < d eff ≤ 100, and semantic/manifold approaches necessary for d eff > 100. Recent advances in mechanistic interpretability, particularly Anthropic's sparse autoencoder work extracting interpretable features from Claude 3 Sonnet, demonstrate partial progress but face logarithmic scaling (Conjecture 3.7) and conjectured irreducible polysemanticity. This unified framework provides rigorous foundations for future XAI research and clarifies the inevitable trade-offs in practical deployment.

title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Industry-Specialized Multi-Agent Systems for Recruitment
affiliations: , Shanghai Zhongqiao Vocational and Technical University, LeapIn Group, LeapIn Group and University of Pennsylvania

detail.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Industry-Specialized Multi-Agent Systems for Recruitment
detail.abstract: AI-driven recruitment systems commonly employ general-purpose models adapted across industries, yet whether industry differences represent minor variation or structural heterogeneity requiring specialized architectures remains unclear. This study analyzes over 100,000 real interviews from eight industries using a 23-dimensional competency framework, examining heterogeneity across three levels: configuration, prioritization, and content. Results reveal substantial divergence: inter-industry competency correlations average 0.36, assessment priorities follow a universal Pareto pattern (top five = 81.7%) yet with dramatically different compositions, and only 28.2% of questions overlap. These findings demonstrate that industries operate under distinct assessment paradigms rather than shared model variants. Industry-specialized multi-agent architectures thus emerge as a structural necessity, since shared models cannot accommodate orthogonal competency structures and non-overlapping content. The three-level heterogeneity framework provides a principled basis for designing specialized AI systems and identifying when architectural rather than parametric adaptation is required.

title: Neutral Point-of-View Operational Language in Earnings Calls and Market Response
affiliations: University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business

detail.title: Neutral Point-of-View Operational Language in Earnings Calls and Market Response
detail.abstract: Operational performance shapes firm value, but granular operations information is rarely standardized in financial statements and is instead conveyed in narratives such as earnings calls. Prior work shows that talking more about operations in calls is associated with higher abnormal returns. This paper asks a complementary question of whether the neutral point-of-view (NPOV) of operations-related language in earnings calls is associated with stock market reactions and analyst forecasts. We use the operations-management (OM) lexicon of Voleti et al. (2025) to identify OM-related sentences in prepared remarks and Q&A, and apply a BERT-based classifier trained on Wikipedia neutrality edits to measure the NPOV of each sentence. Our main OM NPOV measures, OM_NPOV_PR and OM_NPOV_QA, are the average NPOV of OM-related sentences in the prepared remarks and management answers, respectively. We use 80,651 calls for U.S. firms from 2006-2023 and estimate fixed-effects panel regressions with rich financial and textual controls, including sentiment, readability, lexical complexity, and the incidence of OM talk. We find that higher OM_NPOV_PR is associated with higher short-window cumulative abnormal returns around the call, but not with post-call return drift. A one-standard-deviation increase in OM_NPOV_PR is associated with approximately 26 basis points higher CAR(-1, +1), and OM_NPOV_PR explains about one percent of the residual variation in CAR after controls and fixed effects. The association is concentrated in quarters with negative earnings surprises. We do not find strong evidence that OM_NPOV_PR predicts next-quarter sales growth or that it is amplified in periods with positive discretionary accruals, which weakens interpretations that rely on earnings management or private information about future-term fundamentals. On the information-environment margin, higher OM_NPOV_PR is associated with smaller analyst forecast errors when firms exhibit shorter cash conversion cycles or higher inventory turnover. Robustness checks using calibrated NPOV measures, lagged NPOV controls, and placebo tests based on financial and overall NPOV suggest that the neutral style of OM disclosures in prepared remarks captures a distinct dimension of disclosure that investors and analysts respond to in the earnings call window. Our results suggest that neutral, fact-focused OM narratives help investors and analysts process operational information when valuing earnings news.

title: Do Accounting Standards for Revenue Recognition Affect Boards' Performance Evaluation Formula?
affiliations: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Accounting, College of Business, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) and

detail.title: Do Accounting Standards for Revenue Recognition Affect Boards' Performance Evaluation Formula?
detail.abstract: In Holmström (1979), a signal can be informative about agent efforts and yet be noisy. Using Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 606-which replaces rules-based, industry-specific revenue recognition guidelines with principles-based, contract-specific standards-we investigate how boards respond when managerial judgment can render accounting performance a more informative but noisier signal of CEO effort. Using two alternative difference-indifferences models, we consistently find that CEO pay-earnings sensitivity declines after the adoption of ASC 606. Consistent with our view that this decline is driven by increased noise in accounting performance, the effect is concentrated in revenues-the component affected by ASC 606-rather than expenses, and is more pronounced when discretionary revenues are high. The reduction in pay-earnings sensitivity is mitigated when firms have previously provided more conservative and higher-quality earnings, as well as when they disclose disaggregated revenue items. Importantly, our findings remain robust when we capture pay-earnings sensitivity using explicit, formula-based provisions in CEO compensation contracts. We further demonstrate that the decline in payearnings sensitivity mitigates subsequent earnings management, suggesting that boards' contractual adjustments help curb opportunistic reporting under ASC 606. Overall, our findings explore how boards navigate the trade-off between informativeness and noisiness of accounting performance amid rises in managerial judgment in reporting.

title: Aligning Night Shifts with the Chronobiological Rhythm: What Logistics Can Learn from Healthcare to Enhance Workforce Well-Being

detail.abstract: The logistics sector operates day and night just like the healthcare sector. This 24-hour operation ensures delivery reliability and customer satisfaction but places high demands on the employees who keep the system running. Night work is one of the greatest sources of stress in this sector, with negative consequences for health, safety and productivity. At the same time, personnel in logistics are scarce, making retention and employee wellbeing essential for continuity. In recent years the Dutch Healthcare Institute has carried out several pilots in healthcare in which night shifts were aligned more closely with the biological rhythm of employees. Different interventions were introduced to reduce the effects of night work. Recent experiments such as the one in the Jeroen Bosch Hospital show that adapting schedules to the chronobiological system leads to significantly fewer gastrointestinal complaints, less fatigue, better recovery and a likely reduction in absenteeism. This article examines what the logistics sector can learn from this approach. It shows that the human body is a powerful but often overlooked factor in the organization of labour. By designing schedules that align more closely with the biological clock, logistics can not only improve employee wellbeing but also contribute to social sustainability.

title: Contractual Freedom and Public Policy in Syndicated Finance: A Constitutional Approach to Financial Governance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Contractual Freedom and Public Policy in Syndicated Finance: A Constitutional Approach to Financial Governance
detail.abstract:
This paper critically examines the tension between contractual freedom and the principles of public policy within the global syndicated lending market, with a specific focus on its implications for Nigerian infrastructure and finance. Syndicated loans, while vital for funding large-scale developmental projects in Nigeria, are vulnerable to opportunistic actions like "uptiering" transactions, where select lenders subordinate the debt of the remaining syndicate without their consent.

The analysis contrasts the doctrinal responses of major legal systems: New York courts prioritize textualist enforcement, offering high predictability but little protection against innovation that undermines collective trust. English courts, while theoretically allowing a check on discretionary powers (the Braganza principle), remain deeply cautious. The paper argues that Nigerian law, characterized by its strict "sacrosanct" view of contract and absence of robust good faith doctrines, creates a constitutional vacuum where the loan agreement itself becomes the sole source of governance.

To mitigate "lender-on-lender violence" and protect the integrity of the collective investment, the paper proposes a "constitutional design" framework for syndicated finance. This framework is built upon four core principles: Anti-Subordination (requiring unanimous consent for seniority loss), Anti-Conflict Voting (excluding conflicted parties from amendment votes), Carve-Out Integrity, and Rational Discretion. By elevating these safeguards from mere contractual clauses to an explicit constitutional order of private law, the paper argues for a more stable and just market architecture that sustains both development and fairness.

title: The Trust Premium

detail.title: The Trust Premium
detail.abstract: I develop a game-theoretic equilibrium model that microfounds trust as an equilibrium selection mechanism in asset markets. I analyze a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma among investors where trust evolves endogenously through Bayesian updating of beliefs about counterparty types. The model generates multiple Markov Perfect Equilibria: a high-trust cooperative equilibrium with low strategic risk premia, and a low-trust defective equilibrium with elevated discount rates. My central contribution is to formalize how transient coordination failures can trigger self-reinforcing trust decay that propagates through asset prices via an augmented stochastic discount factor. The framework provides microfoundations for trust as a fundamental determinant of financial valuations, independent of cash flow dynamics.

title: CBDC Stress Test in a Dual-Currency Setting

detail.title: CBDC Stress Test in a Dual-Currency Setting

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding received.

detail.abstract:
This study explores the potential impact of introducing a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) on financial stability in an emerging dual-currency economy – Romania, where the domestic currency (RON) coexists with the euro. It develops an integrated analytical framework combining econometrics, machine learning, and behavioural modelling. CBDC adoption probabilities are estimated using XGBoost and logistic regression models trained on behavioural and macro-financial indicators rather than survey data. Liquidity stress simulations assess how banks would respond to deposit withdrawals resulting from CBDC adoption, while VAR, MSVAR, and SVAR models capture the macro-financial transmission of liquidity shocks into credit contraction and changes in monetary conditions.

The findings indicate that CBDC uptake (co-circulating Digital RON and Digital EUR) would be moderate at issuance, amounting to around EUR 1 billion, primarily driven by digital readiness and trust in the central bank. A one-point increase in digital trust raises the likelihood of adoption by approximately 12%. Liquidity simulations show that under a holding cap of RON 7,500 (about EUR 1,500 for the scenario where Digital RON and Digital EUR co-circulate), over 60% of banks could absorb deposit withdrawals without significant stress, selling less than a quarter of their securities portfolios. Beyond RON 15,000, however, nearly 40% of banks would face deposit outflows exceeding 10% of total liabilities, necessitating large-scale asset sales and wholesale funding. Every RON 1 billion in deposit withdrawals is associated with a 0.7–1 – 1.1% decline in credit portfolios. Nonetheless, even in adverse scenarios, the maximum overall liquidity cost to the banking system remains manageable at around RON 2 billion over a decade.

The study concludes that a non-remunerated, capped CBDC – designed primarily as a means of payment rather than a store of value – can be introduced without compromising financial stability. In dual-currency economies, differentiated holding limits for domestic and foreign digital currencies (e.g., Digital RON versus Digital Euro) are crucial to prevent uncontrolled euroisation and preserve monetary sovereignty. A prudent design with moderate caps, non-remuneration, and macroprudential coordination can transform CBDC into a digital liquidity buffer and a complementary monetary policy instrument that enhances resilience and inclusion rather than destabilising the financial system.

title: A Three-Point Model of Reference-Dependent Satisfaction: Integrating Expectations, Opportunity Costs, and Upside Surprises
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Three-Point Model of Reference-Dependent Satisfaction: Integrating Expectations, Opportunity Costs, and Upside Surprises
detail.abstract: We develop a formal model of reference-dependent satisfaction that extends Prospect Theory and expectations-based reference points by introducing three independent reference points: Satisfaction Potential (PS), Base Point (PB), and Dissatisfaction Potential (PI). Unlike existing models that treat satisfaction and dissatisfaction symmetrically through a single value function, we demonstrate that these are fundamentally distinct psychological mechanisms with separate dynamics. Our key innovation is the explicit incorporation of opportunity costs into the reference structure: the value of alternatives not chosen (V₂) shifts the dissatisfaction potential independently of satisfaction potential, weighted by the probability those alternatives would have succeeded (P₂). We prove that the ratio of dissatisfaction to satisfaction (r = I/S) diverges to infinity as subjective probability of success approaches certainty, formalizing why overconfidence creates extreme emotional vulnerability. The model generates novel predictions about decision-making under uncertainty in one-shot decisions, explains classical findings in behavioral economics, and provides a mathematical foundation for wisdom traditions emphasizing "detachment" and managing expectations. We propose five testable predictions and discuss applications to therapy, performance anxiety, and relationship dynamics.

title: AI Salience and the Cost of Equity Capital
affiliations: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE), Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE), Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE) and Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE)

detail.title: AI Salience and the Cost of Equity Capital
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI) salience and the cost of equity capital (COE). We innovatively decompose the AI disclosure during earnings conference calls into two parts: the materialised component: AI capability and the unmaterialised component: AI salience. Utilizing a theoretical framework grounded in game theory, we explore how firms can strategically manipulate AI salience to influence investor perceptions and financing costs. The model predicts that while AI salience can lower the COE by reducing investor uncertainty, it can also increase disclosure noise, leading to a non-monotonic relationship between AI salience and cost of equity. We empirically test this model using earnings conference call transcripts and implied COE data from U.S. firms over the period 2002-2021. Our results indicate that AI salience is negatively correlated with COE, suggesting that firms with higher AI salience enjoy lower financing costs. Furthermore, we demonstrate that institutional ownership and market attention moderate this relationship, with the effect being more pronounced in firms with weak governance and imperfect market competition. The findings highlight the strategic role of AI salience in corporate financing, offering new insights for both investors and regulators in understanding the financial implications of AI disclosures.

Using a 100-acre integrated education hub prototype, the study demonstrates how K-12 schools, universities, medical colleges, residential facilities, and shared infrastructure can be structured within a unified yet flexible financial ecosystem. The framework introduces a CapEx-FAR-Revenue linkage model integrating physical metrics with financial performance drivers, combining entity-wise P&L segmentation, shared-service cost allocation, and dynamic CapEx phasing. Findings show integrated ecosystems achieve 22-25% higher NPV and 3-5 percentage-point IRR uplift versus standalone institutions when supported by shared services and phased development. The Shared-Infrastructure Elasticity Index (SIEI) of 0.153 quantifies that each 1% increase in shared infrastructure investment yields 0.15 pp IRR improvement. For investors, the framework reframes education infrastructure as a predictable quasi-infrastructure asset class; for policymakers, it demonstrates how land-use regulations function as de facto industrial policy.

detail.title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLI-GENCE IN CORPORATE RISK MANAGE-MENT
detail.abstract: In the context of the struggle for technologi-cal superiority, artificial intelligence is be-coming one of the key tools for achieving leading positions. At the same time, scien-tists are engaged in a heated discussion about the feasibility of its use in many areas of our lives and the threats of degradation of human qualities that distinguish them from other representatives of the living world. At the same time, there is an area where the use of this tool is very beneficial, and its dominance over human abilities in this area is beyond doubt. This area includes financial management, or more precisely, the as-sessment and management of risks in the company's activities. Artificial intelligence has already found wide application in risk management in financial intermediation. However, in the real sector, especially in the processing industry, shipbuilding, automobile manufacturing and certain heavy equipment, its use in risk management is only on the agenda. The purpose of the scientific work was to propose approaches to the further development of methods for using genera-tive intelligence to assess and manage risks based on an analysis of the experience of using artificial intelligence in financial man-agement. To do this, the authors updated information on typical risks in financial man-agement, studied the ways of using artificial intelligence to work with these risks, as-sessed its impact on the quality of financial risk management of companies using practi-cal examples, identified the strengths and weaknesses of this approach, and as a re-sult developed recommendations for the further development of the corporate financial management system. The article is of inter-est to practicing economists who are improv-ing approaches to the use of artificial intelli-gence in their organizations, as well as those involved in planning and determining busi-ness development vectors for the near fu-ture. In particular, the authors provide rec-ommendations for overcoming the key prob-lems of introducing artificial intelligence into company risk management, and also em-phasize strategic approaches to its applica-tion, and not just as a technological tool in the current analysis, which is a novelty for published studies.

title: US-Israel Strategic Partnership in Central Asia

detail.title: US-Israel Strategic Partnership in Central Asia
detail.abstract: The article demonstrates that the United States and Israel pursue a similar strategy toward the Central Asian countries that were part of the Soviet Union before its collapse. The most important points of convergence of their shared strategic interests are as follows: countering the nuclear threat from Iran; countering the threats and challenges posed by radical Islam; and limiting the economic and military-political presence of Russia and China in the region, located at the intersection of key trade routes rich in energy resources.

detail.title: Los Efectos Desconocidos detrás de los Aranceles de EE. UU. sobre la economía de Brasil (The Unknown Effects Behind U.S. Tariffs on the Brazilian Economy)
detail.abstract:
Spanish Abstract: Este estudio realiza un examen exhaustivo de la lógica subyacente detrás de la impo-sición de aranceles por parte de los Esta-dos Unidos, particularmente bajo la admi-nistración Trump, sobre la economía de Brasil. El objetivo principal es evaluar las ventajas y desventajas de estas medidas tanto para la economía estadounidense como para el entorno económico global. Para lograrlo, la investigación introduce un modelo innovador de evaluación arancela-ria que adopta una perspectiva más prácti-ca y realista, lo que permite un análisis más claro y sistemático de las intenciones estratégicas que impulsan dichas políticas. Además, el estudio incorpora conceptos y definiciones de reciente desarrollo para mejorar la objetividad y la profundidad del análisis. Finalmente, el recién desarrollado Diagrama de Interconectividad de los Efectos de los Aranceles (TEI-Diagram) introduce conceptos innovadores y un mar-co metodológico sencillo, ambos detalla-dos en la misma investigación. Por último, el TEI-Diagram se aplicó para examinar los efectos de los aranceles de Estados Unidos sobre el comercio internacional de Brasil.

English Abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive examination of the underlying logic behind the imposition of tariffs by the United States particularly under the Trump administration on the Brazilian economy. The main objective is to assess the advantages and disadvantages of these measures both for the U.S. economy and for the global economic environment. To achieve this, the research introduces an innovative tariff-evaluation model that adopts a more practical and realistic perspective, allowing for a clearer and more systematic analysis of the strategic intentions driving such policies. In addition, the study incorporates newly developed concepts and definitions to enhance the objectivity and depth of the analysis. Finally, the newly developed Tariff Effects Interconnectivity Diagram (TEI-Diagram) introduces innovative concepts and a simple methodological framework, both detailed in the study. The TEI-Diagram was applied to examine the effects of U.S. tariffs on Brazil’s international trade.

title: Copyright, Antitrust, and the Politics of Generative AI
affiliations: Pennsylvania State University, Dickinson Law

detail.title: Copyright, Antitrust, and the Politics of Generative AI
detail.abstract:
The rapid ascent of generative artificial intelligence has unsettled the long-standing relationship
between copyright and antitrust law. Copyright, once described as conferring “mini-monopolies”
in expression, contains embedded safeguards such as fair use, the idea–expression dichotomy,
first sale, compulsory licenses, and misuse approximate an internal competition policy. Antitrust,
by contrast, has traditionally operated as an external guardrail, disciplining exclusionary
conduct when market power threatens contestability. This Article advances three claims. First,
copyright’s internal competition policy levers should remain the system’s primary mechanism for
balancing exclusivity and access. Second, because those internal safeguards already mediate
most conflicts between innovation and control, premature or politicized resort to antitrust risks
upsetting that balance, distorting doctrine, and undermining enforcement credibility. Third, the
task is to recalibrate the interface between the two regimes so that antitrust continues to serve
as an external guardrail against demonstrable exclusionary conduct rather than as an instrument
of executive will. A five-pronged strategy defined by regulatory clarity, compliance by design,
institutional reform, policy realignment, and empirical research can help recalibrate the copyright–
antitrust interface in an era of AI-mediated creativity. By situating this analysis within the
context of the Trump administration’s 2025 reorientation of competition policy, the Article shows
why restraint, clarity, and doctrinal humility are essential to sustaining an AI ecosystem that is
innovative, contestable, and just. Recent events illustrate how prosecutorial discretion can be
bent toward executive retribution rather than neutral law enforcement. Antitrust should intervene
only where exclusionary conduct is demonstrable, not as a substitute for copyright’s calibrated
balance or as a vehicle for executive industrial policy.

title: The Stability of Self-Control in Unstable Times
affiliations: School of Economics, University of Sydney, Universite du Luxembourg - Department of Economics and Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research (LISER)

detail.title: The Stability of Self-Control in Unstable Times

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines the stability of self-control over time using nationally-representative longitudinal data from Australia. We track the same individuals between 2019 and 2023, a period encompassing one of the most disruptive global crisis in recent history: the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite these extraordinary circumstances, self-control remained remarkably stable: its mean and distribution were unchanged, and individuals largely preserved their relative positions. Within-person changes were small, and unrelated to variations in state-level exposure to both the spread of the virus and the policy responses that ensued. The evidence we report suggests that self-control is a deeply rooted, trait-like characteristic that persists even under extreme societal stress.

detail.title: Pathology of charity organizations in Iran; With an emphasis on extracting strategies and policies to promote the charity sector using the SWOT technique
detail.abstract: Charities are among non-profit organizations that are not based on personal profit and pursue charitable and public goals. Being non-governmental, non-profit, non-political, voluntary, and independent are common characteristics of public charity organizations. The current research tries to answer these questions using the SWOT technique: What are the weaknesses and threats of charity organizations in the country? And what strengths and opportunities do they benefit from? What strategies can minimize the weaknesses and prevent those threats from causing harm by taking advantage of the strengths and opportunities in charitable organizations? The results of this research, which used the library method in data collection and content analysis in the inferences, and applied CVI and CVR measurement tools in the validity of the results, indicated that by adopting strategies such as the institutionalization of the public sectors of charity affairs with a network approach, institutionalization of the governance sectors of charity affairs with a network approach, cultural and managerial development in the country's charity sector, and the networking of charitable institutions, the existing strengths will be strengthened, the weaknesses of charity organizations will be reduced to the minimum and existing threats will be turned into opportunities.

title: The Ontology of Money: A Unified Theory of Scarcity Regimes

detail.title: The Ontology of Money: A Unified Theory of Scarcity Regimes
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of credible scarcity as the fundamental determinant of monetary value. I develop a unified recursive framework in which money's realness depends on the stability of its scarcity-enforcement process. Within this framework I define a new equilibrium concept-the Scarcity-Stable Equilibrium (SSE)-and prove its existence and global stability under bounded enforcement variance. Analytical and numerical results show that when enforcement variance exceeds a critical threshold, equilibrium multiplicity and sunspot volatility emerge endogenously. The model links algorithmic and institutional forms of money through a single state variable-the credibility of scarcity enforcement-and generates quantitative predictions relating monetary stability to the variance of enforcement policy. Simulations confirm a sharp variance-determinacy frontier and demonstrate that institutional credibility enlarges the stability region. The theory rationalizes why algorithmic monies attain stable valuations while discretionary fiat systems exhibit belief-driven volatility, and it offers design principles for central-bank digital currencies based on optimal scarcity management.

title: Tax Disputes with the IRS Need an Upgrade – More ADR for Better Tax Administration [Tax Analyst/Tax Notes]

detail.abstract:
The article argues that the IRS is undergoing rapid transformation and that modernizing tax administration requires a significant focus on robust ADR coupled with modern technology to make tax administration more efficient, fair, and predictable.  

Because litigation is costly, slow, and prone to inconsistent outcomes, the authors contend that early resolution mechanisms are essential, particularly given shrinking IRS staffing, outdated technology, and growing administrative burdens. They, among other things, recommend prioritizing voluntary disclosures, reopening or modernizing programs like OVDP, and offering settlement initiatives much earlier, especially for abusive or widely marketed transactions.

title: Design Theft In Nigeria's Fashion Industry: Evaluating The Legal And Enforcement Framework For Intellectual Property Protection

detail.title: Design Theft In Nigeria's Fashion Industry: Evaluating The Legal And Enforcement Framework For Intellectual Property Protection
detail.abstract: Fashion is a vital medium of self-expression and a key platform for showcasing creativity across the globe. In Nigeria, the fashion industry has experienced remarkable growth and recognition in recent decades, generating substantial revenue and contributing significantly to cultural identity and economic empowerment. However, this expansion was accompanied by a rise in design theft-the unauthorized replication of original fashion designs without permission or attribution. These copied designs are often sold at lower prices and produced with inferior quality, undermining the creative and economic efforts of original creators. In response to these challenges, this paper seeks to evaluate the adequacy of Nigeria's legal and enforcement frameworks for protecting fashion designs, identify barriers faced in curbing design theft and suggest necessary reforms. It examines the protection offered by key intellectual property regimes applicable to the fashion industry-copyright, trademarks, and industrial designs-as well as the administrative and judicial enforcement mechanisms. The research methodology is doctrinal, drawing from statutes, case law, international instruments and articles. Through legal analysis and case review, the paper identifies key challenges hindering effective protection and proposes practical reforms. Ultimately, this research aims to contribute to the limited body of literature on intellectual property and fashion in Nigeria while offering valuable suggestions for strengthening the legal safeguards against design theft.

title: Monetary Efficiency Ratio (MER): A Novel Indicator for Central Bank Policy
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Monetary Efficiency Ratio (MER): A Novel Indicator for Central Bank Policy
detail.abstract: Central banks face a dual mandate: maintaining full employment while controlling inflation, often without a clear metric to guide policy decisions.Traditional economic gauges, such as inflation indices and employment data, are often influenced by externalities-tariffs, commodity shocks, or other non-monetary factors-that can obscure the effectiveness of monetary policy. We propose a novel metric, the Monetary Efficiency Ratio (MER), which evaluates the efficiency of monetary and fiscal expansion in generating real economic output. By combining changes in GDP, public debt, and broad money supply (M3), MER provides central banks with an objective, policy-oriented measure of economic efficiency, aiding in interest rate and liquidity decisions.

title: Strategic Dynamics of Fintech and Traditional Banking: Competition, Collaboration, and Public Policy Directions

detail.title: Strategic Dynamics of Fintech and Traditional Banking: Competition, Collaboration, and Public Policy Directions
detail.abstract: Fintechs are enabling creative digital services that compete with the traditional financial intermediation offered by banks. Fintech challenges the ways financial firms innovate, and influences competition policy in three critical aspects. First, new digital consumer products and services enable novel ways of delivering financial intermediation. Supervisory authorities must not stifle innovation, and the tools selected must foster growth. Second, the reintermediation of financial markets, services, or products through digital platforms can either increase or lower risks, affecting the choice of regulatory instruments. Third, financial products can be tailored artificially, making competition policy enforcement more complex. Since financial markets are fundamentally different and innovation gravely affects competition dynamics, these aspects merit clear consideration by authorities [1].

title: "Climate-Related Investment Arbitration: Tribunal's Approaches to Rollback of Renewable Energy Incentives" (2025) 22 Transnational Dispute Management 3, TDM Special Issue "International Investment Arbitration - Environmental Protection and Climate Change Issues" (4th volume)

detail.title: "Climate-Related Investment Arbitration: Tribunal's Approaches to Rollback of Renewable Energy Incentives" (2025) 22 Transnational Dispute Management 3, TDM Special Issue "International Investment Arbitration - Environmental Protection and Climate Change Issues" (4th volume)
detail.abstract: This article analyzes how arbitral tribunals have interpreted fair and equitable treatment (FET) standard to disputes arising from the rollback of renewable-energy incentives. Based on a comprehensive case analysis, it maps three approaches the tribunals have taken on whether general legislation can ground legitimate expectations of regulatory stability: a restrained line that considers general legislation does not create specific commitments capable of generating legitimate expectations; a middle-ground that allows changes within an “acceptable margin”; and a more expansive view that reads investment-inducing frameworks plus consistent assurances as commitment-forming. The article also traces two approaches to investor due diligence within the reasonableness inquiry: a stricter view that treats diligence as a prerequisite to any expectations claim, and a broader view that treats diligence as a relevant consideration but not dispositive. Across these strands, tribunals increasingly take a more balanced approach, weighing foreseeability, proportionality, and the investor’s conduct, though with varying intensity. The analysis concludes with practical implications for investors and states based on recent jurisprudence.

title: Religion, Institutional Architecture, and the Europe-China Divergence: A Review Essay on Greif, Mokyr, and Tabellini’s Two Paths to Prosperity
affiliations: George Mason University - Schar School of Policy and Government

detail.title: Religion, Institutional Architecture, and the Europe-China Divergence: A Review Essay on Greif, Mokyr, and Tabellini’s Two Paths to Prosperity
detail.abstract: This review essay engages Two Paths to Prosperity (Greif, Mokyr & Tabellini, 2025) and develops an alternative, mechanism first account of the Europe-China “Great Divergence.” Two Paths to Prosperity explains Europe’s ascent through cultural-institutional coevolution, where corporate forms internalized values that enabled impersonal exchange. This essay reframes that account, using instead a comparative historical model of mechanisms. It argues that the Europe–China divergence hinges on how belief was translated into enforceable cooperation—through distinct architectures of authorization, selection, diffusion, and sanction (ASDS)—rather than on differences in religious and moral creeds alone. The framework reveals a recurring contrast: Europe’s plural corporate ecology scaled trust via lateral incorporation, while China’s lineage–state compact stabilized order via vertical accountability. The result is higher causal resolution and a set of testable implications across regions and regimes.

title: Rethinking Inventory Assumptions: LIFO, Inflation, and Earnings Usefulness
affiliations: ESMT European School of Management and Technology,  and Emory University Goizueta Business School

detail.title: Rethinking Inventory Assumptions: LIFO, Inflation, and Earnings Usefulness
detail.abstract: We document a puzzling pattern: firms abandon LIFO inventory accounting at record rates during inflationary periods, precisely when LIFO's tax benefits peak, contradicting tax-based theories. Analyzing 176 abandonment disclosures since 2003, firms cite improved financial reporting usefulness (not earnings improvement) as their primary motivation; only 2.33% avoid losses and 5% avoid missing forecasts, while the median firm incurs $5.25 million in additional taxes. Consistent with firms' reasoning, we find that LIFO reserve changes (which reconcile LIFO to FIFO earnings) predict stock returns and cash flows beyond reported LIFO earnings. A one standard deviation increase predicts 1.22% higher year-ahead returns. This predictive power doubles during high-inflation periods and strengthens for firms with low inventory turnover and FIFO-using peers. The return predictability traces to fundamentals: LIFO reserve changes predict free cash flows and analyst forecast errors, indicating even sophisticated users struggle with LIFO's complexity. Our findings suggest that managers rationally trade substantial tax costs for information transparency when macroeconomic volatility amplifies accounting distortions. These results inform accounting standard convergence debates and demonstrate how inflation transforms inventory accounting from a technical choice into a fundamental determinant of financial statement usefulness.

title: A Simple Model Of A Court Captured By The Executive Power

detail.title: A Simple Model Of A Court Captured By The Executive Power
detail.abstract: This paper presents a simple analytical model of judicial behavior under executive influence. Judges allocate time between routine, constitution-respecting decisions and spectacular rulings that reinterpret constitutional norms. Executive alignment increases prestige and reduces the institutional cost of such creativity, while media exposure amplifies both effects. The model shows that political capture and visibility jointly push judges toward constitution-bending, performative decisions, eroding efficiency and the separation of powers. A welfare comparison reveals that the socially optimal level of judicial creativity is lower than the judge's private optimum, highlighting how political and reputational incentives can transform the judiciary from an independent institution into an instrument of executive power.

title: Transformation of the Eurozone Architecture Crises and Institutional Change in the Offshore US-Dollar System
affiliations: Global Climate Forum, Freie Universität, Berlin, SOAS University of London and Global Climate Forum

detail.title: Transformation of the Eurozone Architecture Crises and Institutional Change in the Offshore US-Dollar System

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We have no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This study is the result of two research projects funded by Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG). It is the conclusion of the project ‘Hierarchical and Hybrid Money on a Fractured Continent: Europe’s Monetary Architecture after the Eurocrisis’, carried out at the Global Development Policy Center of Boston University (project number 41592217). Moreover, the study is an output of the Emmy Noether research group entitled ‘The Political Economy of Financing Large-Scale Transformations. Off-Balance-Sheet Fiscal Agencies in Wars, Reconstruction, and the Green Transition’ (OBFA-TRANSFORM), hosted at Global Climate Forum Berlin as well as Freie Universität Berlin (project number 499921148).

publicationDetails.detailsText: Boston University, Global Development Policy Center, Global Economic Governance Initiative, GEGI Study, October 2025

detail.abstract:
This study investigates how to describe (RQ1) and subsequently explain (RQ2) the transformation of the Eurozone architecture—in line with the Monetary Architecture framework—during the Global Financial Crisis and the Eurocrisis.

In response to RQ1, the study develops a novel methodology to depict dynamic transformation of instruments and institutions in a credit money system understood as a web of interlocking balance sheets. It connects with an interactive online tool available at https://monetary-architecture.com that follows the dynamics of both crises from endogenous contraction over elasticity provision through inbuilt mechanisms to the setting up of innovation. This reconstruction of the crises it 'true' to the nature of the credit money system where every asset on one balance sheet has to be a liability on at least one other balance sheet, and where monetary transformation refers to an alteration of the asset-liability structures. As a result, the study shows how the circular expansion and contraction dynamics of the financial cycle translate into the 'Darwinian' institutional evolution of a monetary architecture.

In response to RQ2, the study posits that the crises were about the inability to maintain the funding of the volume and types of credit instruments in the monetary architecture. The Global Financial Crisis comprised the inability of funding instruments in the shadow banking system after an initial default of mortgages by highly indebted households in the United States, whilst the Eurocrisis involved the faltering of private and public funding structure for treasury securities in Europe via a series of  'doom loops', precipitated by an overreliance on funding through repo markets and the introduction of inherently procyclical credit ratings for repo collateral. The funding implosion was halted via interventions that provided innovations to the monetary architecture. These comprise the setting up of new contingent instruments to pull credit instruments on (mainly public) balance sheets higher up in the monetary hierarchy, the creation of new off-balance-sheet fiscal agencies as bad banks or suppliers of emergency elasticity, and the reaffirmation of the reciprocal guarantee of the central bank and the treasury as the main balance sheets at the apex of the monetary hierarchy.

Conceptually, the study adopts a systemic view on the international monetary system which in its present configuration is understood as 'Offshore Dollar System'. Rather than thinking of states as subject to 'Westphalian' monetary sovereignty, the study perceives them as monetary jurisdictions that are integrated in the global web of interlocking balance sheets and are subject to countless cross-border connections via the asset and liability structures of credit instruments. Both cannot exist in isolation and are merely subsets to the global monetary architecture which itself is subject to permanent transformation and contestation.

title: Where the Republic Acknowledges the Person: Recognition, Constitutional Proportion, and the Right to Apply for Asylum
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Where the Republic Acknowledges the Person: Recognition, Constitutional Proportion, and the Right to Apply for Asylum

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Praxis Foundry 001 is an independent civic research initiative developing publicly verifiable legislative, jurisprudential, and constitutional methodology.

detail.abstract:
This Article argues that the right to seek asylum in the United States must be understood not merely as a statutory entitlement, but as a constitutional expression of recognition: the moment at which the legal order acknowledges the individual as a person before the law. Congress codified this recognition in 8 U.S.C. § 1158(a)(1), which provides that any person who is physically present in the United States, or who arrives at its borders, may apply for asylum irrespective of manner of entry. When the Executive sought to suspend this threshold right by proclamation, the conflict that followed was not solely administrative or policy-driven. It was constitutional.

Drawing on Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer and Justice Jackson’s tripartite framework, this Article demonstrates that the Executive occupies its “lowest ebb” of authority when acting against explicit congressional enactment. The judiciary’s intervention in the asylum ban litigation is therefore best understood as a restoration of constitutional proportion, not a political judgment.

The analysis advances a broader theoretical point: legitimacy arises from the alignment of care and consciousness in law, expressed here as L = C + ☿. Recognition is the precondition of legal meaning. To preserve the right to seek asylum is to preserve the Republic’s capacity to see the person.

title: Intra-Boundary Field and Boundary-Breaking Innovation A Supercritical Model of Emergent Creativity at Interfaces
affiliations: Fan Ge Institute

detail.title: Intra-Boundary Field and Boundary-Breaking Innovation A Supercritical Model of Emergent Creativity at Interfaces
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the original concept of the Intra-Boundary Field—a generative zone existing within the overlapping boundaries of systems, disciplines, or organizations. Unlike traditional “cross-boundary” or “open innovation” models, it proposes that disruptive innovation emerges from within boundaries, when information, cognition, and energy flows reach a supercritical threshold of tension and interaction.

At that moment, the boundary itself transforms from a barrier into a field of emergence, producing what the author calls Boundary-Breaking Innovation (BBI). This framework unites philosophy, complexity science, and management practice to explain how new structures, meanings, and capabilities can self-organize within the liminal space of tension.

By redefining the boundary as a dual-natured interface—both obstruction and generative field—the paper offers a new theoretical foundation for managing innovation, organization design, and systemic transformation.

title: A Note on Tanneries in Kanpur, Water Pollution in the Ganges, Taxation, and Tax Shifting
affiliations: Rochester Institute of Technology

detail.title: A Note on Tanneries in Kanpur, Water Pollution in the Ganges, Taxation, and Tax Shifting
detail.abstract: In this note, we provide the first game-theoretic analysis of taxation and tax shifting when tanneries in Kanpur, India, that produce leather and pollute the Ganges River are taxed. We model the n ≥ 2 tanneries as a Cournot oligopoly and a specific tax t > 0 is imposed on each unit of leather produced by the polluting tanneries. We first determine the symmetric Nash equilibrium output of leather and its price with the tax. Second, we show that the rate of tax shifting by the polluting tanneries is constant. Third, we discuss how increasing either the number of tanneries or the price elasticity of demand affects the tax shifting that takes place. Finally, we comment on the policy implications of constant tax shifting such as the predictability of the incidence of the tax burden.

It is a theoretical economic and organizational modeling paper using synthetic and non-personal operational data. detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping how software organizations allocate incentives, structure teams, and design sequential delivery pipelines. This paper develops a formal model to analyze where AI substitutes for human contributors, how effort and contract incentives shift, and why replacement risk varies sharply across positions in a sequential team. The framework studies agents, effort choice, project-success technology, principal optimization, and the role of limited AI resources.

Drawing on field data from TeamStation AI’s Nearshore IT CoPilot and the Axiom Cortex™ cognitive-evaluation engine, we examine replacement probabilities, wage effects, and structural protection for specific roles in Latin American software teams. Results show that the final position in a pipeline is most exposed to substitution, middle positions are structurally insulated, and optimal AI allocation is probabilistic rather than deterministic. These findings provide guidance for CTOs seeking to design resilient nearshore pipelines under increasing AI adoption.

title: Optimising Supply Chain Resilience and Efficiency using Artificial Intelligence in Response to Disruptions
affiliations: Tiffin University

detail.title: Optimising Supply Chain Resilience and Efficiency using Artificial Intelligence in Response to Disruptions
detail.abstract: This study investigates the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing supply chain resilience and efficiency during disruptions. Drawing on the Dynamic Capabilities Theory, it evaluates how AI-driven demand forecasting, predictive analytics, and optimization algorithms support supply chain adaptability, continuity, and performance in the face of crises such as pandemics and geopolitical instabilities. Using a quantitative research design, data were collected from 228 firms in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, all of which have adopted AI in their operations. The findings reveal that AI-driven demand forecasting (β = 0.771), AI-powered predictive analytics (β = 0.091), and AI-based optimization algorithms (β = 0.083) significantly and positively influence supply chain efficiency during disruptions. Factor analysis confirmed the strong construct validity of the model, while regression analysis demonstrated a high explanatory power (R² = 0.878). This research contributes a novel, holistic framework that integrates technological, organizational, and human factors, offering actionable insights for businesses aiming to build resilient and agile supply chains. It further recommends adopting advanced AI tools, fostering cross-functional collaboration, and implementing continuous monitoring to sustain long-term supply chain performance.

title: Control Use and Managerial Responsiveness: Evidence from the COVID-19 Outbreak
affiliations: Vienna University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Control Use and Managerial Responsiveness: Evidence from the COVID-19 Outbreak
detail.abstract: This study examines how managers use control systems to support timely responses to adverse environmental change. Using survey data from U.S. managers collected in close temporal proximity to the COVID-19 outbreak, I analyze the timing of internal risk communication and routine adaptation. Consistent with threat-rigidity theory, the results show that diagnostic use is associated with delays, while interactive use supports more timely action. Managers who use controls interactively for open dialogue and adaptive sensemaking before the onset of adverse change can offset the rigidity of diagnostic systems when facing novel threats. However, increases in diagnostic use after the onset are related to faster responses, reducing delays without sacrificing structured analysis and accountability. These findings are useful to understand how managers use control systems to bridge the communication—action gap more quickly, informing the trade-off between formalization and adaptability in building resilience to environmental shocks.

title: The Evolution of Program Management in the AI Age: Emerging Trends and Their Impact on Organizational Agility and Performance

detail.title: The Evolution of Program Management in the AI Age: Emerging Trends and Their Impact on Organizational Agility and Performance
detail.abstract: Program management has long been an anchor discipline for managing complex projects, managing resources, and aligning initiatives with organizational strategy. With the acceleration of the digital age, organizations are under pressure to cope with increasingly complex multi-project environments that require never-before-seen agility, accuracy, and strategic alignment. Though time-tested frameworks like PMI's PgMP and MSP remain effective in unstructured settings, they often fail to help organizations cope with dynamic business circumstances and fast-paced technology shifts. That failure has accelerated the development of AI-powered and agile-derived program management models that interleave automation, predictive analytics, and smart decision-making to hone responsiveness and efficacy. Herein is an investigation of how the technologies of Artificial Intelligence-in the realm of machine learning, natural language processing, optimization techniques, and predictive analytics-are reshaping program management techniques and improving the agility and performance of organizations. By way of empirical data and comparative study, this investigation proves that AI-powered strategies yield dramatic gains in project completion rates, cost effectiveness, and risk minimization. By way of finding, the study sheds light on determining success factors underlying the success of AI adoption and identifies AI-powered program management as an information driver of first-order significance to innovative capability and adaptive flexibility and sustained competitive advantage.

detail.abstract: This document presents a deep-dive analysis into the concept of a blockchain-based operating system (BOS), deconstructed from first principles. We begin by establishing the foundational axioms of both conventional operating systems and blockchain technology, analyzing their core functions, architectural assumptions, and inherent limitations in isolation. From this foundation, we synthesize a new architectural model, reimagining core OS services such as process management, identity, and file systems through the lens of decentralization, cryptographic trust, and consensus. The analysis culminates in an examination of the systemic challenges, primarily performance and scalability, that confront any practical implementation of a BOS. We review several "proto-BOS" projects to ground our theoretical model in real-world examples and conclude with an assessment of the viability of a true BOS-not as a replacement for general-purpose operating systems, but as a foundational layer for a new class of applications where trust, security, and auditability are paramount.

title: Minority Figures: Inequality in Risk Taking
affiliations: McGill University (Desautels) and Tulane University

detail.title: Minority Figures: Inequality in Risk Taking
detail.abstract:
Problem Statement: Operational performance often depends on individuals disclosing private information that carries interpersonal risk -- such as errors, near-misses, or disease symptoms. Thus, individuals frequently withhold this information, with negative consequences for performance. We examine how group composition -- specifically gender diversity -- affects individuals' willingness to take these risks. Building on social identity theory, we argue that group diversity affects individuals' risk-taking behavior through tokenism and social recategorization. Low diversity leads to status concerns for the minority, while majority members face weaker pressure to disclose unless norms shift.
Methodology/Results: We test this theory in a natural experiment: 5,000 students were randomly assigned to groups during a voluntary viral-screening initiative, where participation had both private costs and stigma risk, yet was required for operational planning. Under-represented gender groups were more likely to participate, and their participation did not induce a spillover effect to the gender majority at low levels of diversity. However, compared to single-gender groups, when the minority share exceeded 40% of the group composition, average group information disclosure increases, driven by an increase in the participation of the majority members.
Implications: Our results show that gender composition affects the assignment of the interpersonal risks associated with disclosure. We clarify when diversity does (and does not) support operational goals, while also highlighting that the burden may be unevenly distributed in mixed gender groups. We inform the design of team structures and incentive schemes that support equitable, operationally-relevant information sharing.

detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes global business environments, leadership practices are undergoing significant transformation. This qualitative study examines how leadership styles evolve in organizations that integrate AI technologies, drawing on case insights from Mastercard, Chevron, Citibank, and Deloitte. Drawing on semi-structured interviews, participant observations, and literature review, the research introduces the concept of Augmented Leadership-a blend of strategic foresight, ethical governance, adaptive coaching, and AI literacy. Findings indicate that leaders are shifting from transactional control to roles emphasizing innovation enablement, cultural stewardship, and ethical oversight. The study concludes with a framework for aligning human leadership strengths with machine intelligence capabilities, highlighting implications for leadership development, organizational design, and future research on AI ethics in management.

title: Mining Workers’ Perceptions of the determinants of COVID-19 Safety Climate Management: Evidence from Ghana’s Mining Sector

detail.title: Mining Workers’ Perceptions of the determinants of COVID-19 Safety Climate Management: Evidence from Ghana’s Mining Sector
detail.abstract: Background: Organisational safety management became critical during the COVID-19 pandemic, yet limited research has examined how mining workers perceive safety climate determinants in Ghana's mining sector. Drawing on safety climate theory, this study assessed workers' perceptions of COVID-19 safety climate management determinants within Newmont's operational environment.Methods: Using an explanatory cross-sectional design, primary data were collected from 366 mining workers through a validated Likert-scale survey. Multivariable regression analyses examined demographic effects on safety climate perceptions, while Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) evaluated the direct relationships between perceived determinants and overall safety climate management.Results: Of ten hypothesized determinants, only three significantly influenced safety climate management. Communication on COVID-19 control strategies emerged as the strongest positive predictor (β=0.25, p=0.014), followed by workers' personal appreciation of risk (β=0.214, p=0.026) and supportive environment (β=0.152, p=0.027). Management commitment, supervisor environmental control, worker involvement strategies, rules and procedures, worker competence, and hazard identification showed no significant influence on safety climate perceptions. Multivariable regression analyses revealed that education level and work experience were the strongest demographic predictors of safety climate perceptions across multiple domains.Conclusion: Effective safety climate management in large-scale mining operations during health crises depends primarily on clear communication and workers' risk awareness, challenging conventional assumptions about the primacy of management commitment and formal procedures. These findings offer targeted guidance for policymakers and mining companies to optimize resource allocation and intervention strategies for future health emergencies.

detail.abstract: Environmental turbulence sets the boundary conditions for leadership effectiveness. This paper proposes a plain-English, 10-item checklist to rapidly assess turbulence (score 0-10) and map results to five levels, each paired with a matching leadership operating pattern (decision cadence, planning horizon, teaming, capital allocation, partnering, resilience). We integrate an outside-in view of turbulence with situational leadership's inside-the-firm focus and advance testable hypotheses: (H1) fit between turbulence level and operating pattern improves decision speed, forecast accuracy, pivot success, and resilience; (H2) misfit reduces performance; (H3) leader adaptability buffers misfit costs; (H4) external fit and internal follower/task fit interact positively. We provide a printable diagnostic and a readiness playbook intended for future validation (KR-20, test-retest, convergent/criterion evidence). The contribution is a usable, theory-consistent bridge between environmental reading and leadership action, enabling managers to "lead for their level of turbulence" and giving researchers a compact, testable framework.

detail.abstract:
The rapid and enthusiastic interest in development and deployment of Agentic AI and especially autonomous agents which are capable of independent reasoning, leveraging and  executing tools, has outpaced the definition of governance mechanism that is required to manage their operational, ethical and regulatory risks.There are existing AI governance models like NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, do provide foundational controls however, they are very generic and lack the implementation depth for these conitnuously acting, multi-agent systems.

This paper introduces The Agentic AI Governance Framework, which is a six principled lifecycle model designed to ensure traceability, accountability, and regulatory alignment across agentic deployments. The framework formalizes quantifiable controls through two applied mechanisms: the Agentic Log Retention Index (ALRI), which defines evidenceretention periods based on agent risk and jurisdiction, and a Runtime Governance Architecture integrating human-in-loop escalation, tool-access allow-lists, and modelprovenance capture. Implementation mappings are provided for major orchestration environments including LangChain, Power Platform, and UiPath. 

Adoption of the framework enables organizations to reconstruct agentic decisions within 24 hours, achieve ≥ 95 % provenance coverage, and detect behavioral drift within 10 % variance. The proposed model bridges the current gap between compliance principles and deployable governance practice, establishing a reusable baseline for safe and auditable Agentic AI operations.

title: Air Force Under Fire: Time to Own Base Defense

detail.title: Air Force Under Fire: Time to Own Base Defense
detail.abstract: Missile defense, force protection, and base defense as a whole are common military functions for all the services, and doctrine directs the Air Force to “conduct offensive and defensive ops, to include appropriate air and missile defense, to gain/maintain air superiority.” Army air defense assets will always be stretched thin, its limited assets already committed to supporting other joint and high-priority missions, and many of the Army’s systems are too logistically cumbersome to meet the Air Force’s needs. Therefore, the Air Force must be funded by Congress and the Department of Defense to have some organic, service-retained, capabilities to counter small UASs and cruise missiles to cover the gaps in the joint force’s coverage while also investing in passive defenses and other mitigation measures. The Air Force must also improve its air base ground defense capabilities to meet emerging base defense challenges and to leverage technology to make up for the lack of available manpower.

title: Type-Stratified Forecasting of Medical Supplies: Handling Regular and Irregular Weekly and Monthly Demand
affiliations: University of Technology of Troyes, University of Technology of Troyes, University of Technology of Troyes, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Type-Stratified Forecasting of Medical Supplies: Handling Regular and Irregular Weekly and Monthly Demand
detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Forecasting the demand for medical supplies is essential for patient safety while also being a major challenge in inventory management. Each product exhibits its own stochastic demand pattern, making manual forecasting infeasible at scale. Forecasting models can assist, but they often struggle with sparse, irregular, or bursty demand, especially in hospital settings. The objective of this study is to develop a type-stratified forecasting framework that specifically addresses lumpy and intermittent medical supply demands, improving their forecasts without contaminating models trained on smoother series.Methods: Medical supply series were first classified using the ADI–CV2 taxonomy into smooth, erratic, intermittent, and lumpy categories. Smooth and erratic series were handled by a multioutput regression pipeline, while intermittent and lumpy series were processed through a twostage Classification + Regression pipeline. The first stage predicts demand occurrence using a CatBoostClassifier, the second estimates magnitude using a RandomForestRegressor, and a recurrent-demand mapping layer adjusts predictions toward historically recurrent magnitudes. The approach was evaluated at both weekly and monthly frequencies, with performance measured via nRMSEI, nRMSEII, ROC–AUC, and the cost-sensitive SPEC metric.Results: The proposed pipeline achieved competitive accuracy across all datasets. On intermittent and lumpy series, it reduced event-conditioned magnitude error (nRMSEI) from 0.72 to 0.67 at weekly frequency and from 1.99 to 1.92 at monthly frequency after applying the recurrent-demand mapping. SPEC analysis showed a consistent reduction in shortage-related costs compared to classical models such as ARIMA, Prophet, or Croston, even when nRMSE values were similar. Weekly Updated evaluation provided slightly better performance than Recursive inference, while monthly data also favored the Updated strategy due to error accumulation over longer horizons.Conclusions: The study confirms that segmenting time series by demand type and explicitly modeling occurrence and magnitude substantially improves operational forecasting for medical supplies. The proposed lightweight machine learning pipeline, though less expressive than deep learning architectures, achieves robust performance with low computational cost, making it suitable for on premise hospital deployment without GPU infrastructure. This trade-off between interpretability, energy efficiency, and predictive accuracy represents a pragmatic step toward sustainable and secure AI applications in healthcare logistics.

detail.abstract: We analyze the potential for complexity theory to produce insights that elucidate the evolution of socioeconomic inequality and point toward effective policies. We position complexity theory as a complement to more traditional economic approaches. Economic models of inequality can fall into four broad categories: models based on individual attributes and technologies, social interaction models, intergenerational models of transfer, and models of institutional and social structure. Within each of these categories, complexity theory can enhance traditional theory. It is of particular value in helping to distinguish between bottom-up systemic and top-down structural causes of inequality. Complexity theory can further enrich our understanding of economic inequality by adopting a complex adaptive system of systems approach in which economic, social, political, and psychosocial systems interact with one another and with institutional and social structures to produce robust inequality, particularly on racial lines.

It identifies ten key decisions (D1-D10) and organizes them within a fourstep governance cycle that links theory, fieldwork, and disclosure. By turning methodological choices into documented evidence, SSGM promotes a new culture of research governance-one that values transparency as much as precision.

detail.abstract: The Evolutionary Hybrid Sampling Framework (EHSF) introduces a renewed perspective in survey methodology by merging the inferential rigor of probability sampling with the adaptive versatility of non-probability data. Traditional hybrid approaches often rely on fixed parameters and manual calibration, which can lead to instability and limited reproducibility. In contrast, the EHSF replaces these static mechanisms with an evolutionary optimization process that iteratively learns from the data. By integrating calibration, trimming, and propensity weighting within a multi-objective fitness function, the framework enables the sampling design to self-adjust dynamically until statistical balance is achieved. Ultimately, the EHSF offers a reproducible, computationally efficient, and theoretically grounded responseto the growing representativeness crisis in modern digital surveys.
